events.text: A thin poet in a patched blue robe has drunk your best Dragon Well every afternoon for a month and paid for none of it. Today he asks for a brush instead of the bill, and looks very meaningfully at your clean white wall.

choices.text: Hand him the brush

effects.log: He writes eight lines in one breath, signs them Drunk Crane of the West Lake, and falls asleep on the bench. The ink is still wet when the first scholar stops to read.

choices.text: Hand him the bill

effects.log: He pays in copper, coin by coin, with the face of a man paying for his own funeral, and does not come back. (+12 taels)

choices.text: Let him drink, but keep the wall clean

effects.log: He bows, drinks, and writes his poems on the backs of your order slips instead. The waiters keep them in a drawer.

events.text: A cart of young scholars from the provincial academy stops at your door. They have heard that Drunk Crane's newest poem hangs in a teahouse in this town, and they would like to see it, and to sit under it, and to argue about the fourth line.

choices.text: Charge a little extra for the seats under the poem

effects.log: The tables under the wall are booked for weeks. Scholars quarrel about the fourth line over cup after cup. (+60 taels)

choices.text: Let anyone sit there for the price of tea

effects.log: The teahouse becomes the place where young scholars come to be clever at each other. It is very loud and very good for business.

events.text: The magistrate's secretary arrives with a long face. Someone has read the fourth line as an insult to the magistrate, who has a famously short neck. The secretary suggests the wall be whitewashed by tomorrow.

choices.text: Whitewash it

effects.log: The painter weeps a little as he works. By noon the wall is white and the scholars have gone to drink somewhere braver.

choices.text: Argue that the line is about a heron

ok.log: You recite three classical poems about herons with short necks. The secretary, out of his depth, agrees that it is plainly about a heron.

fail.log: The secretary does not care about herons. The poem stays, but the fine is real. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Hang a silk curtain over the fourth line

effects.log: The curtain only makes everyone lift it. The magistrate pretends not to know. It becomes a town joke, which is safer than a town scandal.

events.text: Years later a letter comes from the capital, in the same wild hand. Drunk Crane has become Hanlin Academician Wen, and he remembers a teahouse wall and an owner who let him drink on credit.

choices.text: Ask for nothing but a new poem

effects.log: He sends a new poem, framed this time, with a seal from the Hanlin Academy. Your teahouse is in the guidebooks now.

choices.text: Ask him to settle his old tab

effects.log: He settles it with interest and a note: "The most honest bill I ever received." (+150 taels)

events.text: A storyteller with a folding fan and a wooden clapper offers to perform in your teahouse for a share of the takings. His speciality, he says, is true stories about people who are still alive.
events.arc: The Storyteller of the Third Table

choices.text: Hire him

effects.log: He starts that night with a tale of a tax collector and a goose. The house is full by the second clap. (+20 taels)

choices.text: Ask him to tell only old legends

effects.log: He sighs, and tells the tale of the White Snake for the thousandth time. He tells it beautifully.

choices.text: Send him away

effects.log: He bows and walks to the teahouse across the street. You hear the laughter from there all evening.

events.text: The storyteller's new series, The Magistrate's Missing Granary, is the talk of the town. The audience stamps for more. A clerk from the yamen has started sitting at the back, writing things down.
events.arc: The Storyteller of the Third Table

choices.text: Tell him to stop the series

effects.log: He ends it with a fire that conveniently burns all the evidence. The audience boos. The clerk stops coming.

choices.text: Let him finish the story

effects.log: The final episode names no names, and everyone knows every name. The teahouse has never earned so much in a month.

events.text: Constables come at dawn for the storyteller. They also come for your ledger, which they want to see is clean.
events.arc: The Storyteller of the Third Table

choices.text: Hide the storyteller in the cellar

ok.log: He is out of the county in a vegetable cart by noon. Months later an inspector from the capital opens the granary and finds it empty.

fail.log: The constables find him behind the pickle jars. You pay a fine for the jars and the storyteller. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Hand him over

effects.log: He goes quietly, fan in hand. Your regulars stop telling you anything.

events.text: The storyteller is back from the next county, older and pleased with himself. The granary scandal has already gone stale; he wants to try something new: the true story of the owner of this teahouse.
events.arc: The Storyteller of the Third Table

choices.text: Agree, if he makes you look good

effects.log: He makes you look very good, and slightly taller. Customers keep asking about the tiger you wrestled.

choices.text: Forbid it

effects.log: He tells it anyway, in another town, where you are a seven-foot hero with a jade fist. People come to see if it is true. (+15 taels)

events.text: An old man in a straw hat sets up a go board in your corner every morning, pays for one pot of tea, and beats everyone who sits down. The losers order more tea to console themselves.
events.arc: The Old Man Who Never Loses

choices.text: Give him his tea free

effects.log: He nods once. From then on, the corner is his, and the losers keep paying for their sorrows.

choices.text: Charge challengers a copper to play him

effects.log: The coppers pile up in a bowl beside the board. The old man does not seem to notice or care. (+25 taels)

choices.text: Sit down and play him yourself

ok.log: You lose by half a point, the closest anyone has come. He looks at you properly for the first time.

fail.log: He finishes you in forty moves and pours you a cup of your own tea. You learn something anyway.

events.text: A provincial go champion in a silk robe arrives with three attendants and a carved board of his own. He has heard of the old man in your corner and has come to put him in his place.
events.arc: The Old Man Who Never Loses

choices.text: Host the match as an event

effects.log: Half the town crowds in. The old man wins by resignation at move one hundred and twelve and goes back to his tea. (+70 taels)

choices.text: Warn the old man and let him decide

effects.log: He shrugs and plays. He wins. The champion leaves the carved board behind and does not come back for it.

events.text: The old man does not come one morning. A boy brings his board, his stones and a note: the teahouse has been kind, and he is going to the mountains to die where the pines are. The note is signed with the name of a go saint everyone thought was dead.
events.arc: The Old Man Who Never Loses

choices.text: Keep the board in the corner, set up as he left it

effects.log: People come for years to look at his last game. Nobody dares to move a stone.

choices.text: Go after him into the mountains

effects.log: You find him under a pine, alive and annoyed. He plays you one last game in the snow and sends you home with the answer to a problem you did not know you had.

events.text: The old man does not come one morning. A boy brings a note: he did not enjoy being sold by the copper, and has taken his board to the teahouse across the street, where they give him his tea for nothing.
events.arc: The Old Man Who Never Loses

choices.text: Go over and apologise

effects.log: He accepts the apology, but not the invitation back. Your losers follow him across the street.

choices.text: Shrug and hire a go teacher instead

effects.log: The teacher is very correct and nobody wants to play him. The bowl of coppers stays empty. (-30 taels)

events.text: A monk from a mountain monastery leaves a sample on your counter: a pinch of grey-green leaves that smell of rain on stone. Cloud Fog, he says. The monastery grows forty catties a year and has never sold any to a town.

choices.text: Brew it at once

effects.log: The first cup tastes of the inside of a cloud. Your tea master sits down without asking and does not speak for a while.

choices.text: Offer a price for the whole harvest

effects.log: The monk counts the silver twice, apologises for counting it twice, and promises the harvest by the spring. (-100 taels)

events.text: Cloud Fog is the talk of the town. The rich order it by the pot and send their servants back for more. The monastery's next letter is less humble: the abbot would like twice the price, or the leaves will go to the Plum Pavilion instead.

choices.text: Pay the new price

effects.log: You pay. The rich keep paying more. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Go up the mountain and talk to the abbot

ok.log: You sweep the courtyard with the novices and drink tea with the abbot until midnight. The price stays as it was, and you are invited back.

fail.log: You arrive with a cold and leave with a worse one. The leaves go to the Plum Pavilion.

choices.text: Let the Plum Pavilion have it

effects.log: The Plum Pavilion puts out a huge sign for Cloud Fog. Your regulars drift over to try it.

events.text: A merchant from the coast offers you a hundred catties of "Cloud Fog" at a tenth of the price. It smells mostly of the sack it came in.

choices.text: Throw him out

effects.log: He goes to the Plum Pavilion next. Two months later their customers are complaining about the taste of sacks.

choices.text: Buy it and mix it in

effects.log: Nobody notices for a season. Then the tea master notices, says nothing, and quietly gives notice. (+90 taels)

events.text: Two men in the back booth think the clatter of the teahouse hides their voices. It does not hide them from you. They are talking about the county granary, a moonless night, and how many carts the bandits of Black Pine Ridge will need.

choices.text: Tell the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate listens with half an ear and promises to double the watch. You are not sure he means it.

choices.text: Pretend you heard nothing

effects.log: You refill their pot. One of them tips well, which feels worse than it should.

choices.text: Sell what you heard to a rival gang

effects.log: The rival gang pays well and asks no questions. (+60 taels)

events.text: On the moonless night the bandits come for the granary.

choices.text: Go and stand with the watch

roll.foeName: the bandits of Black Pine Ridge

ok.log: The watch was doubled after all, and you are in the front of it. The bandits run into the paddies. The town remembers who warned it.

fail.log: You hold the gate long enough, and pay for it in bruises. The grain is saved.

choices.text: Bar your own door and wait

effects.log: In the morning the granary still stands. The watch caught them at the bridge, on your word.

events.text: On the moonless night two gangs fight over the county granary, and in the morning half the grain is gone and the street is full of broken carts. The magistrate wants to know who knew what.

choices.text: Keep your head down

effects.log: Nobody can prove anything, but the town is a small place. Fewer people come for tea.

choices.text: Pay the families who lost grain

effects.log: You pay quietly, through the temple, so nobody knows it was you. You know. (-80 taels)

events.text: Your best server, Little Plum, and your cook, Big Wu, have not spoken in a week. The cause is a purple-clay Yixing teapot, eighty years old, now in three pieces. Each says the other broke it.

choices.text: Make them mend it together

effects.log: They sit at opposite ends of the bench with a pot of rice glue between them, insulting each other in whispers. It is a start.

choices.text: Dock both their wages

effects.log: Now they agree on one thing: you. (+10 taels)

choices.text: Say you broke it yourself

effects.log: Both of them know you did not. Both of them stop arguing at once.

events.text: A pottery mender of the old kind is passing through: a woman who fills cracks with gold lacquer so that the break becomes the most beautiful part of the pot. She turns the three pieces over in her hands and names a price.

choices.text: Pay her to make it whole

effects.log: The pot comes back with three golden rivers across it. Little Plum and Big Wu argue now about who gets to pour from it. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Keep the pieces in a box

effects.log: The box sits on the shelf. Sometimes Big Wu opens it and looks inside, and closes it again.

events.text: Little Plum and Big Wu come to you together, which has never happened before. They are getting married, and they would like to hold the wedding tea in the teahouse, with the golden pot.

choices.text: Close the teahouse for a day and give them the wedding

effects.log: The whole street comes. Big Wu cries into the noodles. Little Plum pours the first cup for you. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Give them the evening, and keep the day for business

effects.log: The wedding is small and loud and very happy. You make a little money that day, too. (+20 taels)

events.text: Three days of rain, and the river is in the street. Your teahouse stands on old cedar stilts, the only dry floor on the waterfront. People are wading towards it with children on their shoulders.

choices.text: Open the doors to everyone

effects.log: By night there are ninety people on your floor and every kettle is boiling. Nobody pays. Nobody is asked to.

choices.text: Let people in for the price of a pot of tea

effects.log: Most of them pay. The ones who cannot pay stand on the steps in the rain. (+50 taels)

events.text: On the second night the water is up to the top step and one of the stilts groans like an old man getting out of bed.

choices.text: Dive in and brace the stilt with a beam

ok.log: You come up blue with cold and the floor stops leaning. Ninety people cheer, quietly, so as not to shake anything.

fail.log: The stilt goes. The kitchen end of the teahouse slides into the river with the stove and the stock, but the floor where people stand holds.

choices.text: Move everyone to the far end and pray

ok.log: The stilt groans all night and holds. At dawn the water starts to fall.

fail.log: The kitchen end goes into the river at dawn, with the stove. Nobody is in it.

events.text: When the river goes down, the town counts what it lost and who sheltered whom. A procession arrives at your door with a red banner: Ninety Lives Under One Roof. The magistrate is at the back, trying to look as if it were his idea.

choices.text: Hang the banner over the door

effects.log: The banner hangs for twenty years. People bring their visitors to drink under it.

choices.text: Ask the magistrate to rebuild the levee instead

ok.log: With ninety witnesses behind you, he can hardly refuse. The new levee is called the Teahouse Bank.

fail.log: He promises, and forgets. The banner goes up anyway.

events.text: When the river goes down, the town remembers the steps, and the people who stood on them in the rain.

choices.text: Give a year of free tea to everyone you turned away

effects.log: Some come and drink. Some never set foot in the place again. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Say that a business is a business

effects.log: It is true. It is also what the town calls you, for years.

events.text: The teahouse is too small for the people who want to sit in it. A carpenter called Lu the Ninth offers to raise a second floor with a balcony over the river, in a style he calls 'cranes resting'. He shows you a model made of chopsticks.
events.arc: A Second Floor Over the River

choices.text: Build it his way

effects.log: Lu the Ninth and his three sons start at dawn. The chopstick model sits on your counter as a promise. (-150 taels)

choices.text: Build something plain and cheap

effects.log: A box on top of a box. It keeps the rain off. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Wait a year

effects.log: The crowd waits on the steps. Some of them wait at the Plum Pavilion instead.

events.text: The new floor is finished. Upstairs, under the 'cranes resting' eaves, you can see the whole bend of the river. Officials and rich merchants ask for the private rooms by name.
events.arc: A Second Floor Over the River

choices.text: Keep the private rooms for those who pay most

effects.log: The upstairs makes more than the downstairs within a season. You hear a great deal that you were not meant to. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Keep one table on the balcony for anyone at all

effects.log: The balcony table is never empty: a fisherman one day, a prefect the next. The town loves it.

events.text: The plain box upstairs leaks in the autumn rain onto the heads of the people downstairs. A regular holds up an umbrella indoors, as a joke, and soon everyone is doing it.
events.arc: A Second Floor Over the River

choices.text: Call Lu the Ninth to fix it properly

effects.log: He fixes it, and adds a little crane on the ridge, for free, out of pride. (-90 taels)

choices.text: Lean into the joke: Umbrella Teahouse

ok.log: You hang painted umbrellas from the ceiling. It becomes the strangest and most famous teahouse in the county.

fail.log: It is funny once. Then it is wet.

events.text: Every morning the waiters find three copper coins on the corner table by the window, though nobody sat there and the doors were barred all night. The waiters will not wipe that table any more.
events.arc: The Coins at the Empty Table

choices.text: Sit up one night to watch

ok.log: Near the fourth watch a small old woman lets herself in through the loose kitchen shutter, sits at the table, sips cold tea from yesterday, and leaves three coins.

fail.log: You fall asleep. You wake with a crick in your neck and three coins on the table, and a shawl over your shoulders that is not yours.

choices.text: Burn incense and leave it alone

effects.log: The coins keep coming. The waiters feel better. The table becomes the ghost table, and people ask to see it.

events.text: The woman at the table is Granny Fang, whose son drowned forty years ago the night before he was to open a teahouse here. She has been coming since the building went up, for one cup at his table.
events.arc: The Coins at the Empty Table

choices.text: Leave a fresh pot out for her every night

effects.log: The next morning the coins are gone and there is a paper flower on the table instead.

choices.text: Invite her to come in the daytime

ok.log: She comes on a Tuesday, very straight, in her best jacket, and drinks a hot cup for the first time in forty years.

fail.log: She is embarrassed to have been seen, and stops coming. The table is very empty without her coins.

events.text: Granny Fang has died in her sleep. Her neighbours bring you a small box she left for the teahouse: forty years of copper coins, three for every night, and the deed to the plot of land where her son meant to build.
events.arc: The Coins at the Empty Table

choices.text: Name the corner table after her son

effects.log: A small wooden plaque goes up: The Table of Fang the Younger. Nobody sits there without saying good morning first.

choices.text: Use the coins for her funeral, and build on the land

effects.log: You give her the funeral her son would have. On his land, a little pavilion goes up where the poor can drink tea for nothing. (+80 taels)

events.text: The Tea Guild of the prefecture sends its master's nephew to inspect your scales. He is nineteen, wears four rings and finds, after a short look at nothing, that your scales are wrong. The fine can go away for a small gift.

choices.text: Pay the gift

effects.log: He pockets it without counting. You suspect you will see him again. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Have the scales checked by the yamen

ok.log: The yamen weighs a silver ingot on your scales and on theirs. Yours are right to a hair. The nephew leaves without his gift.

fail.log: The yamen clerk is the nephew's drinking friend. Your scales are wrong. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Pour him tea and talk about something else

effects.log: He is so surprised that someone wants to talk to him that he forgets the fine. He comes back on his own, to talk.

events.text: The guild master's nephew is back, with friends. This time it is your tea leaves: impure, he says. This time the gift is larger.

choices.text: Take it to the Guild Master himself

ok.log: The Guild Master is old and tired and very fond of good tea. He drinks yours, sighs, and sends the nephew to count crates in a warehouse in the north.

fail.log: Blood is thicker than tea. Your guild seal is suspended for a season.

choices.text: Pay again

effects.log: It is cheaper than a quarrel with the guild, this year. (-80 taels)

events.text: The nephew turns up alone, ringless, with his robes muddy from the road. His uncle has died, and the guild has thrown him out. He asks, very quietly, whether you need anyone to wash cups.

choices.text: Give him a job

effects.log: He washes cups badly for a month and well for ten years. He turns out to be very good with the difficult customers.

choices.text: Wish him well and send him on

effects.log: You give him a few coins for the road. He bows lower than he ever has. (+5 taels)

events.text: A guest in a wide bamboo hat takes the corner room, pays a month in advance in clean silver, eats alone and never once takes off the hat, not even to sleep, according to the girl who brings the hot water. His sword is wrapped in grey cloth.
events.arc: The Guest Who Never Took Off His Hat

choices.text: Leave him in peace

effects.log: He leaves a little extra silver on the tray each morning, as if to say thank you for not asking.

choices.text: Try to see his face

ok.log: From the roof beam you glimpse a scar from brow to jaw, and a face that is on a wanted poster in the next county.

fail.log: The beam creaks. The hat tilts up very slightly towards you. You decide to go back to the kitchen.

events.text: Four bounty hunters arrive at dusk, wet and loud, asking about a swordsman with a scar. The poster on the table between them says three hundred taels. The guest in the corner room has not come down for supper.
events.arc: The Guest Who Never Took Off His Hat

choices.text: Tell them the room number

effects.log: They pay you a hundred for the number. You hear the fight upstairs, and then a window breaking, and then nothing. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Say no such guest stays here

ok.log: They grumble, eat four bowls of noodles each, and ride on before dawn. The hat comes down to breakfast as usual.

fail.log: They do not believe you and search the inn. The corner room is empty, the window open. Two tables are broken.

choices.text: Warn the guest and let him choose

effects.log: He listens, nods, and walks down the stairs to meet them. The bounty hunters suddenly remember an appointment somewhere else.

events.text: A letter arrives with no name on it, only a drawing of a bamboo hat. Inside, the story: the scar came from the son of a prefect, the poster from the prefect, and the swordsman has just cleared his name before the Martial Alliance.
events.arc: The Guest Who Never Took Off His Hat

choices.text: Pin the hat drawing above the bar

effects.log: Word gets around that the Bamboo Hat stayed at your inn. Wanderers come from three provinces to sleep in the corner room.

choices.text: Write back and ask him to visit

effects.log: He comes the next spring, hat in hand, and you see his face at last. It is a very ordinary, very tired face.

events.text: A year later, a man with a scar from brow to jaw stands at your counter, very much alive, and asks for the corner room. He does not take off his hat.
events.arc: The Guest Who Never Took Off His Hat

choices.text: Give him the room, and say nothing

ok.log: He comes for you at the third watch. You are awake. It ends on the stairs, with neither of you dead and him gone into the rain.

fail.log: He takes back the hundred taels and some of your pride on the way out. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Pay him back the hundred taels and apologise

effects.log: He weighs the silver, and then you, and leaves. It was the right price. (-100 taels)

events.text: Your cook, Auntie Song, makes a pork-bone broth that takes three days and a secret she will not tell even you. Travellers plan their journeys to stop at your inn for it. The owner of the Golden Duck down the road has noticed.
events.arc: The Broth That Takes Three Days

choices.text: Raise her wages before anyone else can

effects.log: Auntie Song is surprised and pleased, and pretends to be neither. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Ask her for the secret, for safety

ok.log: She tells you, in a whisper, after making you swear on the kitchen god. It is so simple that you nearly laugh, and so you never will.

fail.log: She looks at you as if you had asked for her teeth. The broth is a little thinner that month.

choices.text: Do nothing

effects.log: Things are fine as they are. Probably.

events.text: Auntie Song comes to you with a letter in her apron. The Golden Duck offers her twice what you pay, a room of her own and a kitchen boy to carry the bones.
events.arc: The Broth That Takes Three Days

choices.text: Match the offer

effects.log: She stays. The broth stays. The Golden Duck sends you a very polite New Year card. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Tell her you cannot, and that you hope she stays

ok.log: She says she was only curious what she was worth, and that she is not going anywhere. Then she charges you for the letter.

fail.log: She goes. Travellers go with her, down the road to the Golden Duck.

events.text: The Golden Duck has a new cook and a new sign, Three-Day Broth, but the broth tastes of one afternoon. Auntie Song, still in your kitchen, tastes a spoon of theirs that a traveller brought over, and spits it into the fire.
events.arc: The Broth That Takes Three Days

choices.text: Let her go and cook there for one day, to show them

effects.log: She cooks one pot in their kitchen in front of their cook and walks out without a word. The Golden Duck takes the sign down.

choices.text: Put up a sign of your own: The Original

effects.log: Customers who have tried both are your best advertisement. (+30 taels)

events.text: Guests in Room Seven keep asking for another room in the middle of the night. They hear scratching in the walls, and someone sighing, and once a voice that said, quite clearly, the word 'fish'.

choices.text: Hire a Taoist exorcist

effects.log: Master Qiu arrives with a peachwood sword, a bell and a bill. He chants for an hour and declares the room very haunted indeed. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Sleep in Room Seven yourself

ok.log: At midnight the scratching starts, then the sighing, then, quite clearly, a small voice: "Mrrow." It is coming from inside the wall.

fail.log: You do not sleep at all, and something in the wall seems to be laughing at you. In the morning you notice a hole near the floor.

choices.text: Rent it cheap as a haunted room

effects.log: Young wanderers pay to sleep there on a dare. (+20 taels)

events.text: You pull a board off the wall of Room Seven. Behind it is a very fat orange cat, a nest of fish bones and three kittens. The cat looks at you with deep contempt.

choices.text: Keep them as the inn cats

effects.log: The cat moves into the kitchen and runs it. The kittens are given to good homes. Room Seven is the quietest room in the inn.

choices.text: Tell the story to every guest

effects.log: The Ghost of Room Seven becomes a favourite tale on the post road. The cat is always in it, and always fatter.

events.text: Master Qiu is back. The haunting, he says, has grown stronger: he will need a larger fee and three days. Meanwhile the scratching in Room Seven has been joined by tiny new scratchings.

choices.text: Pay him

effects.log: He chants for three days. The new scratchings get louder. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Pull a board off the wall instead

effects.log: A fat orange cat and three kittens. Master Qiu says he was about to suggest it, and leaves very quickly.

events.text: A caravan from the western deserts wants every room you have for the whole winter: forty men, forty camels and a caravan master called Old Rahim who pays in silver and raisins.

choices.text: Give them the whole inn

effects.log: The yard smells of camels until spring. The silver is very good silver. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Give them half, and keep half for travellers

effects.log: Old Rahim grumbles and accepts. Half of the yard smells of camels. (+70 taels)

events.text: In the middle of winter, a camel eats the magistrate's wife's prize chrysanthemums, which were in pots outside the yamen, which is next door. The magistrate is not amused.

choices.text: Pay for the chrysanthemums

effects.log: You pay for every flower. Old Rahim pays you back in raisins, which is not the same. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Send Old Rahim to apologise in person

ok.log: Old Rahim gives the magistrate's wife a western rug and tells her a story about a camel and a king. She laughs for the first time in years.

fail.log: The magistrate does not want a story. He wants a fine. (-30 taels)

events.text: Spring. Old Rahim's caravan loads up to go west. He asks whether you would like to send goods of your own with them, to be sold in the markets beyond the Jade Gate.

choices.text: Send a cart of tea and silk

effects.log: The cart goes west with the camels. You will not hear of it for a long time. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Wave them off and keep your silver

effects.log: Old Rahim presses a bag of raisins into your hands and promises to come back.

events.text: A dusty boy with a camel stick finds you. Old Rahim's caravan is back from beyond the Jade Gate; your cart was sold in a city whose name you cannot pronounce, and here is what it came to.

choices.text: Count it

effects.log: Silver, a small glass bottle, and a letter from Old Rahim saying he has booked your whole inn again. (+320 taels)

choices.text: Send it straight back west with him

effects.log: Half for you, half for another cart. Old Rahim laughs and says you have the soul of a camel driver. (+120 taels)

events.text: Disciples of the Kongtong Sect sit at one table, disciples of Emei at the other, and between them is a long history and a short temper. Your waiter is carrying the soup the long way round.

choices.text: Seat them in separate rooms

effects.log: It costs you a private room you could have rented. Nobody breaks anything tonight.

choices.text: Bring both tables the same wine, on the house

effects.log: They glare at each other over the same wine. It is hard to fight over the same wine. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Let them settle it themselves

effects.log: You go into the kitchen and close the door. Then you hear the first bench break.

events.text: The common room is wreckage: four benches, two tables, a screen painted with cranes and the big jar of plum wine. The two sects have left, each blaming the other, and neither has paid.

choices.text: Send the bill to both sects

ok.log: Each sect pays the whole bill, so as not to look poorer than the other. (+90 taels)

fail.log: Neither sect answers. You pay for the carpenter yourself. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Go to the Kongtong hall and collect in person

ok.log: The senior disciple pays after the second exchange of blows, and laughs, and says you should have been a martial artist. (+70 taels)

fail.log: You come home with a black eye and no silver, and a story that makes the kitchen laugh.

events.text: Months later the two sects send their senior disciples to make peace, and of all the places in the province, they choose neutral ground: your inn, because both of them once drank the same wine there.

choices.text: Host the peace dinner

effects.log: The peace holds, mostly. Your inn becomes the place where sects meet when they want to stop fighting.

choices.text: Charge them for the privilege

effects.log: They pay without blinking. Peace is expensive. (+120 taels)

events.text: The snow comes down for four days and closes the pass. Inside your inn: a magistrate on his way home, a jade merchant, two monks, a travelling actor and a quiet young woman with ink-stained fingers. On the second night the merchant's jade seal is gone.

choices.text: Search every room

effects.log: Everyone is offended, and nothing turns up. The magistrate writes something in a little book.

choices.text: Watch and say nothing

ok.log: The actor has new rouge on his cuffs. The monks eat meat when they think nobody looks. The young woman goes out into the snow every night and comes back with nothing in her hands.

fail.log: You notice nothing. Everyone is tense. The merchant offers a reward.

events.text: On the fourth night the merchant, red in the face, accuses the actor. The actor accuses the monks. The magistrate, warming his feet, asks you what you think.

choices.text: Say it is the young woman with the ink

effects.log: She looks at you with such contempt that you know you are wrong. The magistrate shrugs and does nothing.

choices.text: Say it is the merchant himself

ok.log: The seal is sewn into his own sleeve: he means to claim it stolen and the debt it secured cancelled. The magistrate is delighted. So is the young woman, who is his creditor.

fail.log: He is furious, and you are wrong, or cannot prove it. The snow melts the next day and everyone leaves in a hurry.

choices.text: Say nothing until the snow melts

effects.log: The snow melts. The guests leave. The seal, you suspect, leaves with one of them.

events.text: The young woman with ink-stained fingers comes back in spring. She was writing all the time, she says: a book of detective tales set in a snowbound inn. She would like to call it after your inn.

choices.text: Agree, gladly

effects.log: The book sells in every market town. Readers come to see the common room and argue about who sat where.

choices.text: Ask for a share of the profits

effects.log: She laughs and pays. The book is called The Inn Without a Name. (+60 taels)

events.text: Workmen digging a new cellar under your inn break into an old brick vault. Inside are twelve sealed wine jars, the clay stamped with the name of a wine house that closed sixty years ago.

choices.text: Open one

effects.log: The wine is the colour of amber and smells of autumn. You have a small cup and sit down rather suddenly.

choices.text: Keep them sealed and tell the guild

effects.log: The wine guild sends an old taster who weeps when he reads the stamps.

events.text: A man arrives claiming to be the great-grandson of the old wine house's owner. The jars, he says, are his.

choices.text: Give him the jars

effects.log: He loads them onto a cart, then hands two back. "For the inn that found them," he says.

choices.text: Ask him for proof

ok.log: He has none. He is a cousin of your cook's friend. You sell four jars to the guild instead. (+150 taels)

fail.log: He has a genealogy and a lawyer. You pay his fees for wasting his time. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Offer to sell the wine together and split it

effects.log: He likes the idea. The wine sells in the capital for a fortune. (+100 taels)

events.text: You keep one jar back, sealed in the new cellar. Years later a famous wine poet hears of it and travels a hundred li to beg one cup.

choices.text: Open it for the poet

effects.log: The poet drinks, writes four lines on your wall and leaves. The lines are quoted in the capital by autumn.

choices.text: Keep it for a better day

effects.log: The poet goes away sad. The jar waits in the dark.

events.text: Your stable boy, Little Tiger, is eleven and can leap from the yard to the stable roof without a run. The guests think it is very funny. A visiting martial artist does not laugh.
events.arc: The Stable Boy Who Could Jump

choices.text: Teach him a little yourself

effects.log: You teach him stances in the yard after dark. He is better than you were at his age, which is annoying.

choices.text: Keep him working the stables

effects.log: He is a very good stable boy. He looks at the guests' swords a lot. (+10 taels)

events.text: A recruiter from Mount Hua stops at the inn, watches Little Tiger jump the wall with a bucket in each hand, and asks who the boy belongs to.
events.arc: The Stable Boy Who Could Jump

choices.text: Let him go to Mount Hua

effects.log: He leaves the next morning with a bundle and a new pair of shoes you bought him. The stables are very quiet.

choices.text: Say he is needed here

effects.log: The recruiter leaves. Little Tiger does not speak to you for a month.

events.text: A young Mount Hua swordsman in plum-blossom robes rides into your yard and leaps from the saddle straight onto the stable roof, just to show you. Little Tiger has come back to visit, with half his sect behind him.
events.arc: The Stable Boy Who Could Jump

choices.text: Throw a feast

effects.log: Mount Hua disciples stop at your inn on every journey for years after. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Make him muck out the stables, for old times

effects.log: He laughs and does it, in his plum-blossom robes. The horses remember him.

events.text: The post-road inspector, a round man called Deputy Gao, informs you that officials on imperial business are entitled to free rooms at any inn on the road. He produces no document, but several officials.

choices.text: Give them the rooms

effects.log: They eat as if imperial business were very hungry work. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Ask to see the regulation

ok.log: There is a regulation. It says free water and a stable, not rooms. Deputy Gao is red to the ears.

fail.log: He reads you a regulation that may or may not exist, very fast. You give them the rooms. (-40 taels)

events.text: Deputy Gao is back with twice as many officials, all on imperial business, all very hungry.

choices.text: Write to the prefect

ok.log: Your letter is so elegant that the prefect reads it aloud at a banquet. Deputy Gao is moved to a post where there are no inns.

fail.log: The letter goes nowhere. Deputy Gao has heard about it.

choices.text: Keep feeding them

effects.log: You feed them. Your other guests eat what is left. (-70 taels)

events.text: A dusty official with a single servant stops for a night and pays full price without being asked. He is the new Inspector of the Post Road, and he asks, mildly, whether anyone has ever demanded free rooms of you.

choices.text: Tell him about Deputy Gao

effects.log: He writes it down. You never see Deputy Gao again.

choices.text: Say no, never

effects.log: He looks at you for a long moment, then pays and goes.

events.text: Wild Goose Pass has no inn at all, only a broken shrine where travellers freeze to death every winter. A branch of yours there would cost a great deal and make very little, at first.
events.arc: A Branch at Wild Goose Pass

choices.text: Build at the pass

effects.log: Masons haul stone up the pass all summer. By the first snow there is a roof, a stove and a lamp in the window. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Put a stove and firewood in the shrine instead

effects.log: It is not an inn, but it is warm. Travellers leave notes of thanks on the wall. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Leave the pass alone

effects.log: The pass is not your business. It is somebody's, surely.

events.text: The first winter at Wild Goose Pass. Your manager there writes that a caravan of salt merchants has been snowed in for twelve days and is eating everything, and that wolves have been seen on the road.
events.arc: A Branch at Wild Goose Pass

choices.text: Ride up yourself with supplies

ok.log: You come through the snow with three mules and no wolves. The salt merchants swear to stop at your inns forever.

fail.log: The wolves take one mule. You arrive with two, and a bandaged arm, and the merchants cheer anyway.

choices.text: Send porters and pay them double

effects.log: The porters get through. Your manager writes that you are a good owner. (-60 taels)

events.text: Spring at Wild Goose Pass. The salt merchants have told everyone. Every caravan going north now plans its road around your inn at the top of the pass.
events.arc: A Branch at Wild Goose Pass

choices.text: Expand the branch

effects.log: A second stable, a bigger kitchen, and a bell for foggy days. It pays for itself in two years. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Keep it as it is, a warm room at the top of the world

effects.log: It stays small. Nobody has frozen at the pass since. That is enough.

events.text: The Zhou and the Lin families have booked your inn for a wedding banquet: thirty tables, two roast pigs and a lion dance. The two families hate each other, which is why the wedding is a peace treaty.

choices.text: Seat the families mixed together

effects.log: You draw the seating chart four times. Every Zhou sits next to a Lin. It looks like a battle map.

choices.text: Seat them on opposite sides of the hall

effects.log: A wide aisle runs down the middle of the hall like a border.

events.text: The night before the banquet, the groom climbs out of a window at your inn and disappears into the rice fields. The bride's family is already in the courtyard, and they are Lins.

choices.text: Go after the groom

ok.log: You find him in a ditch, crying. He is not running from the bride. He is running from the speech.

fail.log: You lose him in the dark, and your shoe in the mud.

choices.text: Stall the families with the lion dance

effects.log: The lion dancers dance for two hours. The families are suspicious but well fed. (-30 taels)

events.text: The banquet goes ahead. The groom gives his speech with his knees shaking, the bride laughs at the right moment, and when a Zhou uncle and a Lin uncle reach for the same duck, they share it.

choices.text: Let the inn be known as the place for difficult weddings

effects.log: For years afterwards, feuding families book your hall to make peace. It is good for business and better for the county.

choices.text: Give the couple the bridal room for free

effects.log: They come back every anniversary. (-20 taels)

events.text: The banquet goes ahead without a groom. The Lins blame the Zhous, the Zhous blame your inn, and by the end of the night both families are blaming each other in a hall full of broken tables.

choices.text: Find the groom the next morning and make him apologise

effects.log: He apologises to everyone, in order of seniority. It takes three hours. The wedding is held again in a month, at your inn.

choices.text: Send both families the bill for the tables

effects.log: They pay, and never book your inn again. (+50 taels)

events.text: A red fever runs through the lower town in the hottest week of summer. The physicians all prescribe the same decoction, and the price of honeysuckle and forsythia doubles by morning. Your drawers are full of both.
events.arc: The Summer of the Red Fever

choices.text: Keep your prices as they were

effects.log: The queue reaches the end of the street. You sell out by noon and weigh out the last of it with your own hands.

choices.text: Sell at the new price

effects.log: Everyone pays. Some of them pay with their wedding silver. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Give it free to the lower town, sell dear to the upper

effects.log: The rich grumble and pay. The poor are given paper twists of herbs at the back door. (+60 taels)

events.text: A grain merchant called Hu has bought every catty of honeysuckle in three counties and is holding it in a warehouse until the fever peaks. He offers to sell you some, at ten times the price.
events.arc: The Summer of the Red Fever

choices.text: Buy what you can and sell it at cost

effects.log: It nearly empties your strongbox. The lower town will not forget it. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Find a substitute herb

ok.log: Dandelion root and isatis, in the right proportion, do nearly as well. Hu's warehouse is suddenly full of very expensive weeds.

fail.log: Your substitute does very little. You keep trying, late into the night.

choices.text: Report Hu to the magistrate for hoarding

ok.log: The magistrate, whose own children are sick, opens the warehouse with a crowbar.

fail.log: Hu dines with the magistrate on Tuesdays. Nothing happens, except that your licence is inspected twice.

events.text: The fever breaks with the first autumn rain. The lower town comes to your door with a lacquered board: Benevolent Hands, Living Pharmacy. Merchant Hu's warehouse is being sold off, cheaply.
events.arc: The Summer of the Red Fever

choices.text: Hang the board and buy the warehouse

effects.log: The board goes over your door. The warehouse becomes your drying room. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Hang the board and leave Hu to his ruin

effects.log: People cross the street to buy from you for a generation.

events.text: The fever breaks with the first autumn rain. In the lower town they have a name for you now, and it is not a kind one. Someone has scratched it into your door.
events.arc: The Summer of the Red Fever

choices.text: Paint over it

effects.log: It comes back every month, in a different hand.

choices.text: Open a free clinic one day a month

effects.log: Some come. Most only stare. It will take years. (-50 taels)

events.text: A farmer from the hills unwraps a damp cloth on your counter. Inside is a gnarled root the size of a baby, with a face, arms and something like a beard. He says it is a thousand-year ginseng. He would like five hundred taels for it.

choices.text: Examine it closely

ok.log: The rings on the neck, the bitterness on the tongue, the faint smell of pine: it is real, perhaps three hundred years old, which is still a marvel.

fail.log: You cannot tell. It might be a ginseng. It might be a very ambitious turnip.

choices.text: Offer fifty taels and see what he says

effects.log: He wraps it up and walks out. He will be back, or he will not.

events.text: You buy the root for two hundred taels and a promise that the farmer may bring you every strange thing he finds in the hills. Now a sect elder, a rich widow and a general's steward all want it.

choices.text: Sell it to the general's steward

effects.log: The general's old mother walks for the first time in a year. The general sends a banner. (+450 taels)

choices.text: Make it into pills and sell them one by one

ok.log: Thirty pills of Three-Century Ginseng Essence. They sell for a fortune each. (+600 taels)

fail.log: The furnace runs too hot. You save nine pills out of thirty. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Keep it for a day when someone truly needs it

effects.log: It sits in a sandalwood box in the back room, slowly drying.

events.text: The farmer from the hills is back, very proud of himself. He has dug up something even bigger. It is, unmistakably and triumphantly, a turnip.

choices.text: Buy it anyway, for luck

effects.log: You put it in the window. The farmer is so happy that he brings you a real mountain herb every season for years. (-5 taels)

choices.text: Tell him the truth, gently

effects.log: He laughs until he cries and leaves the turnip as a gift. Your cook makes soup.

events.text: A child is carried into your pharmacy, grey-lipped, with a fever that will not break. The physician who brought her says only a strong ginseng will hold her until the crisis passes.

choices.text: Use the root you kept

effects.log: You slice it thin and brew it all night. At dawn she asks for congee. Her parents are fishermen; they pay you in fish for twenty years.

choices.text: Sell the family a lesser ginseng

effects.log: It is not enough. She lives, but the fever takes a long time to leave. You do not open the sandalwood box. (+20 taels)

events.text: Your apprentice, a cheerful boy called Peanut, has relabelled every jar in the back room in a single afternoon, alphabetically, as he understands the alphabet. Nobody now knows which jar is which.
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Mixed the Jars

choices.text: Spend the night sorting them by smell and taste

ok.log: By dawn every jar is right, and you know your stock better than you ever have. Peanut sleeps through it.

fail.log: By dawn most jars are right. You are not sure about three of them.

choices.text: Close for a day and make Peanut sort them

effects.log: He works until midnight, weeping onto the angelica. (-20 taels)

events.text: A regular, old Granny Xu, comes back with her cough mixture. It is not the usual one, she says. It is better. Her cough is gone, and so, she says, is her knee pain, which she has had for thirty years.
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Mixed the Jars

choices.text: Work out what went into it

ok.log: One of the three uncertain jars was not loquat but a root from the south. You write the recipe down. Granny Xu's Knee Mixture sells for years.

fail.log: You never work it out. Granny Xu tells everyone you are a genius anyway.

choices.text: Give Peanut the credit

effects.log: Peanut is unbearable for a week and very careful for the rest of his life.

events.text: Peanut has grown up. He wants to open a little pharmacy of his own in the next town, and he asks, nervously, whether you would mind.
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Mixed the Jars

choices.text: Give him a set of your jars, labelled properly

effects.log: He hangs your name under his on the sign. Pupil of the House of the Golden Scales. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Ask him to stay as your manager instead

effects.log: He stays, for now, and runs the back room like a general. He is very good.

events.text: A famous physician, Gu of the Nine Needles, opens a clinic directly across the street with a pharmacy of his own. His patients now buy their herbs from him. He bows to you very correctly in the mornings.

choices.text: Bow back, and lower your prices

effects.log: He lowers his. You lower yours. The street enjoys it very much. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Offer to supply his clinic

ok.log: He is a physician, not a shopkeeper, and hates counting stock. He signs at once. (+60 taels)

fail.log: He thanks you, and refuses, and buys in a second drying rack.

choices.text: Learn needles from watching him

effects.log: You spend your quiet hours at the window, watching how he holds a wrist.

events.text: A rich man collapses in the street between your doors. Physician Gu runs from his side, you from yours, and you both kneel at the same moment.

choices.text: Let him work, and fetch what he asks for

effects.log: He calls for herbs, and you have them in his hand before he finishes the word. The rich man lives. Gu looks at you differently afterwards.

choices.text: Treat the man yourself

ok.log: You are faster. The man lives, and so does your reputation. Gu bows to you, not quite correctly, for the first time.

fail.log: Gu pushes you aside and saves him. The street saw it all.

events.text: Physician Gu is getting old, and his hands shake. He crosses the street one evening with a box of needles and a book of notes, and asks whether the two houses might become one.

choices.text: Join the clinic to the pharmacy

effects.log: The two signs come down. One goes up: Gu and Partner, Clinic and Pharmacy. The street is a little sad to lose its feud.

choices.text: Thank him, and keep your houses apart

effects.log: He leaves the book anyway. You read it every night for a year.

events.text: A pale young man in good clothes asks for arsenic, for rats. He wants enough for a great many rats. He does not look like anyone who has ever seen a rat.

choices.text: Sell it, and note his face

effects.log: He pays too much and does not wait for change. (+10 taels)

choices.text: Sell him chalk, labelled arsenic

effects.log: He takes it without looking. You are fairly sure no rats will die tonight.

choices.text: Refuse him

effects.log: He goes red and leaves. You see him going into the pharmacy at the end of the street.

events.text: News in the morning: old Master Kong of the salt warehouse has been taken ill at dinner, and his nephew, a pale young man in good clothes, is very upset about it.

choices.text: Go to the magistrate with what you know

effects.log: The magistrate is very interested in the chalk. Master Kong recovers from his indigestion. The nephew is sent to explain himself.

choices.text: Go to Master Kong himself

ok.log: He listens, goes very quiet, and changes his will that afternoon. A gift of silver reaches you the next day. (+100 taels)

fail.log: He does not believe you. He believes it a month later, when the nephew tries again.

events.text: News in the morning: old Master Kong of the salt warehouse has died at dinner. The magistrate's clerk is going from pharmacy to pharmacy with a list of who sold arsenic this week.

choices.text: Tell the clerk the truth

effects.log: You describe the nephew. He is arrested. You are fined for selling poison without a witness, and you pay it gladly. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Say your ledger shows no arsenic

effects.log: The clerk looks at your ledger, then at you. He writes something down. The nephew inherits the salt warehouse.

events.text: An old herb-gatherer tells you, over a bowl of noodles, that the Heavenly Snow Lotus on Cold Crane Cliff will bloom this winter, for the first time in twelve years. One flower is worth a pharmacy's year.
events.arc: The Snow Lotus on the Cliff

choices.text: Mount an expedition

effects.log: Ropes, iron spikes, two porters and the old gatherer, who insists on coming. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Promise the old gatherer a share if he goes alone

effects.log: He takes your rope and your promise and goes up the mountain whistling.

events.text: Cold Crane Cliff. The lotus is there, a white star on a ledge sixty feet down, in a wind that wants to pull you off.
events.arc: The Snow Lotus on the Cliff

choices.text: Climb down for it

ok.log: Your fingers are numb, your knees are bleeding through your trousers, and the lotus is in a box against your chest.

fail.deathCause: fell from Cold Crane Cliff reaching for a snow lotus
fail.log: The rope swings. The wind takes your hat, then your footing, then the rope burns through your hands. You come up without it.

choices.text: Let the old gatherer guide the rope, and go slowly

ok.log: It takes half the day. The old man swears all the way through it. You come up with the lotus.

fail.log: The weather turns. You come down the mountain empty-handed, with the old man's words in your ears: twelve more years.

choices.text: Turn back: no flower is worth a fall

effects.log: The old gatherer spits over the edge and agrees with you, which is somehow worse. You go home with all your fingers.

events.text: The Heavenly Snow Lotus sits in your back room in a box of ice. A sect lord, a dying abbess and the court each want it. The old herb-gatherer only wants to see what you will do.
events.arc: The Snow Lotus on the Cliff

choices.text: Give it to the dying abbess

effects.log: The abbess of Emei lives eleven more years. Her nuns buy every herb they need from you, for ever.

choices.text: Sell it to the court

effects.log: A palace eunuch carries it away in a gold box. You never learn who ate it. (+600 taels)

choices.text: Refine it into a pill for yourself

ok.log: One pill, clear as ice. Your meridians feel like a river in spring.

fail.log: The furnace takes most of it. What is left is still something.

events.text: The old herb-gatherer comes back in a month, thinner, with frostbitten fingers and a box. The lotus is in it.
events.arc: The Snow Lotus on the Cliff

choices.text: Give him half of the price

effects.log: He bites the silver and laughs, and says nobody ever gave him half before. You sell the lotus for the rest. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Give him the small share you promised

effects.log: He nods and leaves without a word. You sell the lotus and feel oddly poor. (+300 taels)

events.text: A customer from the next county complains that your Golden Scales Liver Pills did nothing for him. You look at the box. It has your seal, almost. It was never made in your back room.

choices.text: Go to the next county and find the forger

ok.log: A back alley, a mould for your seal, and a family of five rolling flour pills by lamplight.

fail.log: You find nothing but a lot of inns. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Change your seal and post a notice

effects.log: A new seal with a hidden mark. The notice warns against imitations. (-30 taels)

events.text: The forger is a widower with four children who used to roll pills for a pharmacy that closed. He has never hurt anyone, he says: they are just flour and a little licorice.

choices.text: Hand him to the magistrate

effects.log: He gets a year. His children go to an aunt. The fakes stop.

choices.text: Hire him to roll real pills for you

effects.log: He is the fastest pill-roller you have ever seen. The children run errands. You make more pills than ever.

choices.text: Make him swear to stop, and leave him be

effects.log: He swears on his wife's tablet. The fakes stop. You wonder what he does now.

events.text: Every morning beggar children sit on the step of your pharmacy because the stone is warm from the drying room underneath. One of them has an ear infection; another limps.
events.arc: The First Day of the Month

choices.text: Treat them, quietly

effects.log: Garlic oil for the ear, a poultice for the leg. They come back the next day with friends. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Shoo them off the step

effects.log: The step is clean. Customers do not have to step over anyone. (+5 taels)

events.text: There are thirty children on your step on the first of the month. Word has spread through every bridge and alley.
events.arc: The First Day of the Month

choices.text: Make the first of every month a free clinic day

effects.log: You hire a second apprentice. The first of the month becomes the busiest and poorest day of your year. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Ask the temple to share the cost

ok.log: The abbot agrees, and sends two monks to help. The clinic day becomes the temple's pride.

fail.log: The abbot says he will pray about it. You treat the children anyway, this month.

events.text: Years of first days. One of the beggar children from the step comes back as a young physician in a clean grey robe, and asks to work on the first of the month without pay.
events.arc: The First Day of the Month

choices.text: Give the clinic day to the young physician

effects.log: The step is never empty. The young physician brings two more of the old step children to help.

choices.text: Make the young physician a partner

effects.log: The pharmacy grows, and the new partner never lets anyone forget whose step it was. (-50 taels)

events.text: At midnight the drying room catches fire: a lamp, a cat, a rack of dried chrysanthemum. Smoke pours out under the door. Inside are your rare stock and, on the shelf by the window, twenty years of ledgers and prescriptions.

choices.text: Save the rare stock

ok.log: You come out with the ginseng boxes and the musk, coughing. The ledgers burn.

fail.log: You get half the boxes out before the roof beam comes down.

choices.text: Save the ledgers

effects.log: You come out with an armful of ledgers and your eyebrows singed. The stock burns.

events.text: Your neighbours help you rebuild. With the ledgers gone, though, you do not know who owes what, and the debtors are very quiet.

choices.text: Forgive every debt

effects.log: You announce it at the market. Half the debtors pay anyway, out of shame. The other half buy only from you, for ever.

choices.text: Rebuild the books from memory

ok.log: You sit up for a month with an abacus and remember almost everything. (+120 taels)

fail.log: You remember the big debts and forget the small. (+30 taels)

events.text: Your neighbours help you rebuild. The stock is gone, but with the prescriptions saved, physicians from three towns send their patients to the one pharmacy that still has their records.

choices.text: Keep copies in the temple from now on

effects.log: The monks keep a copy of every prescription in a stone vault. It costs you a donation every year and buys you peace.

choices.text: Restock with credit from the herb merchants

effects.log: The herb merchants trust you because of the ledgers. The pharmacy is open again in a month. (-80 taels)

events.text: The Qingcheng Sect needs wound salve and qi-restoring pills for three hundred disciples, every month, and the steward who comes down the mountain asks whether you can make that many.
events.arc: A Contract with the Qingcheng Sect

choices.text: Promise quantity

effects.log: You hire four pill-rollers and run the furnaces day and night. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Promise quality, and a smaller number

effects.log: The steward frowns and agrees to try you for a season. (+60 taels)

events.text: Qingcheng disciples fight a long skirmish with mountain bandits. Your salve is on every wound.
events.arc: A Contract with the Qingcheng Sect

choices.text: Go up the mountain to see how it is holding

ok.log: It is holding well. The sect elder in charge of the infirmary asks for your recipe and you refuse, and he respects you for it.

fail.log: Some batches have spoiled in the heat. The steward is grim. You lose a season of the contract.

choices.text: Trust it and stay home

effects.log: The steward pays the month's bill without comment. (+40 taels)

events.text: The Qingcheng steward is back with a new proposal: the sect wants you as its sole supplier, and in return, you will sell nothing to its rivals of Emei.
events.arc: A Contract with the Qingcheng Sect

choices.text: Accept

effects.log: Qingcheng silver flows in. Emei buys elsewhere, and says so loudly. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Refuse: a pharmacy heals anyone

effects.log: The steward is offended, and comes back a month later to renew the old contract anyway.

events.text: Yan Shisan, a swordmaster with one grey eyebrow and a famous temper, lays a sack of silver on your anvil. He wants a sword that will not break against the Iron Fan of the Southern Wastes. Two smiths have tried. He broke both swords himself.

choices.text: Accept the commission

effects.log: He leaves the silver and says he will come back in a season to break whatever you make. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Refuse politely

effects.log: He snorts and takes his silver to the next town, where, you hear, he breaks a third sword.

events.text: The first blade is ready. Yan Shisan picks it up, sights down it, and swings it once against your anvil.

choices.text: Hold your breath

ok.log: The blade rings and holds, and the anvil gets a notch. Yan grunts. "Too stiff. It will shatter in the cold. Again."

fail.log: The blade snaps a hand from the hilt. Yan hands you the pieces. "Again."

choices.text: Tell him to swing it at something else

effects.log: He swings it at your gatepost instead. The gatepost loses. "Too stiff," he says. "Again."

events.text: The second blade. You have folded the steel a hundred times and quenched it in the river at dawn, the way your grandmother's teacher did. Yan takes it out into the yard and stays there for a long time.

choices.text: Go and see

ok.log: He is crying, very quietly, beside the well. "It sings," he says. He names it Autumn River and pays you twice.

fail.log: He brings it back with a nick in the edge from the well stone. "Good," he says. "Not great." He pays the rest and leaves.

choices.text: Leave him alone with it

effects.log: At sunset he comes in, puts more silver on the anvil than he owes, and walks out with the sword without a word.

events.text: News from the south: Yan Shisan met the Iron Fan of the Southern Wastes on a bridge over the Xiang River. The fan broke. The sword did not. Everyone wants to know who forged Autumn River.

choices.text: Raise your prices

effects.log: Swordsmen queue in your yard. You could forge for ten years and not clear the list. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Take one apprentice from the queue instead

effects.log: The strongest arm in the queue belongs to a ferryman's daughter. You teach her everything Autumn River taught you.

events.text: Your best smith, Old Tie, refuses to teach the new apprentice, Fourth Sister Ma, anything but sweeping. Swords are not for girls, he says. She sweeps very hard and watches everything.
events.arc: The Smith Who Would Not Teach Her

choices.text: Order him to teach her

effects.log: Old Tie teaches her, badly, on purpose. She learns anyway.

choices.text: Teach her yourself after hours

effects.log: You stay late at the forge with her. You find you remember things you had forgotten.

choices.text: Leave it to them

effects.log: She sweeps. He hammers. Nobody talks.

events.text: Old Tie's back gives out in the middle of a rush order: forty spear-heads for the county garrison, due in three days. Fourth Sister Ma asks to take his place at the anvil.
events.arc: The Smith Who Would Not Teach Her

choices.text: Let her

ok.log: She works three days and nights. The garrison captain picks a spear-head at random and finds no fault in it.

fail.log: She finishes thirty-eight on time and two a day late. The captain grumbles and pays anyway. (+20 taels)

choices.text: Do it yourself

effects.log: You finish them with blistered hands. Fourth Sister Ma watches every blow. (+40 taels)

events.text: Old Tie limps into the forge with a parcel wrapped in oilcloth: his own hammer, black with forty years of use. He puts it down in front of Fourth Sister Ma and walks out without a word.
events.arc: The Smith Who Would Not Teach Her

choices.text: Make her a master smith

effects.log: She hangs the hammer over her anvil. Within a year girls from three villages are asking to sweep your forge.

choices.text: Throw a feast for both of them

effects.log: Old Tie gets very drunk and tells everyone that he taught her everything. She lets him. (-30 taels)

events.text: A soft-spoken man with very clean hands orders fifty spear-heads and two hundred arrowheads, cash in advance. He will not say who they are for. Everybody knows that the Red Ridge bandits have been recruiting.

choices.text: Take the order

effects.log: The silver is good. You try not to think about where it came from. (+180 taels)

choices.text: Take the order and tell the garrison

ok.log: The garrison captain smiles and asks you to deliver them on time. (+180 taels)

fail.log: The clean-handed man has a friend in the garrison. He cancels the order with a look you will remember.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: He nods as if it does not matter. Two days later your coal delivery does not arrive.

events.text: The delivery day. The garrison captain's men lie in the reeds by the river ford where the cart is to be met.

choices.text: Drive the cart yourself

ok.log: The bandits come for their spears and get the garrison. The county talks of nothing else for a month.

fail.log: An arrow finds your shoulder before the soldiers rise out of the reeds. The bandits are taken; you are carried home.

choices.text: Send a driver and stay away

effects.log: The trap is sprung. Nobody mentions your name, which suits you.

events.text: Red Ridge bandits raid the salt road with new spears. A survivor says the spear-heads had a little mark stamped on the tang, like the one you stamp on all your work.

choices.text: Go to the magistrate first

effects.log: You confess and pay the fine. The magistrate is surprised you came. It saves you from worse. (-60 taels)

choices.text: File the marks off your stock and say nothing

effects.log: Customers start asking questions. You start losing them.

events.text: A shepherd brings you a stone that fell burning out of the sky into his pasture three nights ago. It is black, pitted and very heavy, and when you strike it, it rings like a bell.
events.arc: Iron That Fell from the Sky

choices.text: Buy it for a fair price

effects.log: The shepherd goes home with silver and a story. You go into the forge with the star. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Tell him it is just a rock

effects.log: He sells it to you for a handful of copper and a sack of salt.

events.text: Star iron will not melt in an ordinary fire. It needs a furnace so hot that the bricks glow white and an anvil that will not crack under it.
events.arc: Iron That Fell from the Sky

choices.text: Build a new furnace

effects.log: It takes a month of brick-laying and a fortune in charcoal. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Feed the fire with your own qi

ok.log: For three hours you pour qi into the bellows. The star softens like wax.

fail.log: The qi comes back up your arms like fire. You will have to try again with bricks.

events.text: The star iron is on your anvil, dark silver, cold as winter after an hour in the fire. Your hammer is waiting.
events.arc: Iron That Fell from the Sky

choices.text: Forge a sword

ok.log: A long sword with a grey ripple like a night sky. Sect masters ride for days to look at it.

fail.log: A good sword, not a great one. The star is only so patient.

choices.text: Forge a plough and a hundred needles

effects.log: The plough never rusts. The needles never break. The village never forgets.

choices.text: Forge a ring for the shepherd

effects.log: He wears it to his wedding. His grandchildren still argue about who gets it.

events.text: The shepherd is back, with an angry nephew who knows something about rocks. The village says you cheated an old man.
events.arc: Iron That Fell from the Sky

choices.text: Pay him what it was really worth

effects.log: He forgives you on the spot. The nephew does not. (-150 taels)

choices.text: Throw them both out

effects.log: The village stops bringing you its hoes.

events.text: A cavalry quartermaster rides into your yard at a gallop. The army marches north in thirty days. It needs two thousand horseshoes and the nails to go with them.

choices.text: Take it all

effects.log: Two thousand horseshoes. You do the sums twice, and then you hire every smith in the county. (+220 taels)

choices.text: Take what you can do well: a thousand

effects.log: He scowls, but takes it. (+100 taels)

events.text: Day twenty. You are short four hundred shoes and the charcoal is running out.

choices.text: Work through the nights

ok.log: You sleep in the coal shed in snatches. The last shoe goes into the crate on the twenty-ninth day.

fail.log: You collapse on the twenty-fifth night. You are still a hundred shoes short.

choices.text: Buy shoes from a rival forge and stamp them

effects.log: They are not your work. They will do. (-80 taels)

events.text: The army has come back from the north. A cavalry officer rides into your yard with a horse that kept its shoes through three hundred li of frozen mud.

choices.text: Ask for the next contract

effects.log: He signs on your anvil. Your yard becomes an army forge for a while. (+160 taels)

choices.text: Ask for nothing, and shoe his horse for free

effects.log: He tells the whole regiment. Soldiers bring their horses to you for years.

events.text: The army has come back from the north, with the horses lamed in the frozen mud and a quartermaster with a list of names. Yours is on it.

choices.text: Pay the penalty

effects.log: It eats every copper the contract paid. (-150 taels)

choices.text: Argue that the order was impossible

ok.log: The general, who once was a smith's son, agrees. The quartermaster is quietly removed.

fail.log: He does not care. You pay. (-150 taels)

events.text: The Iron Family's forge across the river cuts its prices below yours every spring. This year their eldest son, Iron Bao, challenges you to a forging contest at the fair: whoever loses closes for a year.
events.arc: The Forging Contest at the Spring Fair

choices.text: Accept

effects.log: The fair committee is delighted. Posters go up on every wall.

choices.text: Accept, but change the stakes to a feast

effects.log: Iron Bao laughs and agrees. Nobody has to close. Somebody has to cook.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: Iron Bao tells the fair you are afraid. His prices drop again.

events.text: The fair. Two anvils on a stage in front of the temple, a stick of incense, and one task: a kitchen cleaver that can cut a hanging silk scarf.
events.arc: The Forging Contest at the Spring Fair

choices.text: Forge for an edge

ok.log: Your cleaver parts the scarf with no sound at all. Iron Bao's parts it too, a little later. The crowd roars.

fail.log: Your scarf catches on the edge and hangs there. The crowd groans.

choices.text: Forge for beauty

ok.log: It cuts the scarf and it is beautiful. The judges, being people, vote for beauty.

fail.log: It is beautiful and it is blunt.

events.text: You have lost, and the stakes were real. Iron Bao comes to your shuttered forge and stands awkwardly in the doorway.
events.arc: The Forging Contest at the Spring Fair

choices.text: Ask to work at his forge for the year

effects.log: You learn the Iron Family's quenching. He learns your folding. Neither says so.

choices.text: Take the year to travel

effects.log: You visit forges in three provinces. You come back with ideas.

events.text: Iron Bao takes his loss well, or at least loudly. A season later he comes to you with a proposal: one guild seal, two forges, no more price wars.
events.arc: The Forging Contest at the Spring Fair

choices.text: Join the forges

effects.log: The two families eat together at New Year now. The county gets better iron at a fair price. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Shake hands, but stay separate

effects.log: The price war ends. The friendship begins.

events.text: A widow from the ferry crossing brings you a sword in two pieces, wrapped in a quilt. It was her husband's. Her son will be sixteen next spring and wants to join a sect, and she cannot afford a new blade.
events.arc: The Broken Sword of the Ferryman's Widow

choices.text: Reforge it for nothing

effects.log: You weld the break and fold it twice for luck. She tries to pay you in fish.

choices.text: Reforge it at cost

effects.log: She pays in copper, counted out of a cloth purse. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Tell her it cannot be mended

effects.log: You sell her a cheap new sword instead. She thanks you, which is worse. (+20 taels)

events.text: In the steel near the break you find something strange: a name engraved under the guard, filled with old lacquer. It is the name of a sect swordmaster who vanished twenty years ago with a treasure.
events.arc: The Broken Sword of the Ferryman's Widow

choices.text: Tell the widow

effects.log: She turns very pale. Her husband never told her where he came from.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself and finish the sword

effects.log: The widow's son leaves for the mountains with his father's sword and his father's secret.

events.text: The widow's son comes back from Mount Wudang in his second year of training. The sect recognised the sword. His father, it turns out, ran away from them to marry, and the treasure was only the sword itself.
events.arc: The Broken Sword of the Ferryman's Widow

choices.text: Let him tell you everything over tea

effects.log: He is welcomed at Wudang as the son of a lost disciple. He sends his mother silver every month.

choices.text: Ask him to send sect customers your way

effects.log: Wudang disciples start bringing you their swords to be mended. (+80 taels)

events.text: The new silk merchant next door has hired a lawyer. Your hammering starts at dawn, he says, and his wife is a delicate sleeper. He wants the forge closed until the second hour of the morning.

choices.text: Agree to start later

effects.log: You lose half a morning's work every day. The merchant sends a box of cakes. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Refuse: the forge was here first

effects.log: He goes to the magistrate. You go back to your anvil, louder.

choices.text: Muffle the anvil with sand and leather

ok.log: The ring becomes a thud. The work is as good. The merchant sleeps.

fail.log: The muffled anvil gives worse work and no less noise.

events.text: The magistrate summons both of you. The silk merchant's lawyer has prepared a long scroll; you have brought nothing but your hands, which are black.

choices.text: Invite the magistrate to watch the forge at dawn

ok.log: He comes, watches the sparks over the river in the grey light, and rules that the town needs its smith more than its sleep.

fail.log: He comes, gets ash on his robe, and rules for the merchant. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Settle quietly with the merchant

effects.log: You pay to build him a thicker wall. (-40 taels)

events.text: The silk merchant knocks on your gate at dawn with his delicate wife. Robbers came over his wall last night; the ring of your hammer at first light sent them running. He has brought tea.

choices.text: Accept the tea

effects.log: He sits on an anvil and drinks it. From then on he says your hammer is his watchman.

choices.text: Ask him to buy you a better bellows

effects.log: He laughs and buys it. (+40 taels)

events.text: A merchant returns a sword you sold him. It cut his hand when he drew it, then his son's, then his steward's. It is cursed, he says, and wants his money back. Your other customers are listening.

choices.text: Give him his money back

effects.log: He leaves, glad. The sword lies on your counter. Nobody will touch it. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Draw it yourself, in front of everyone

ok.log: It slides out cleanly. You see the problem: the guard is a hair too narrow, and an untrained hand slides forward onto the edge.

fail.log: It cuts you too. Somebody in the crowd gasps "cursed".

events.text: The cursed sword is the talk of the market. Customers cross the street rather than walk past your door.

choices.text: Widen the guard and sell it as The Sword That Bites Fools

effects.log: A swaggering young swordsman buys it at once, to prove he is not a fool. He comes back with a bandaged thumb and a sense of humour.

choices.text: Take it to the temple to be blessed

effects.log: The monks bless it in a long ceremony. Nobody is cut by it again, though you did widen the guard the night before. (-15 taels)

events.text: Years later a scarred, cheerful swordmaster rides into your yard and slaps the old cursed sword down on your counter. He has carried it through forty duels, he says, and it has bitten him exactly once, on the first day, which was the lesson.

choices.text: Offer to buy it back for the wall

effects.log: He sells it back for what he paid. It hangs over your door, and children dare each other to touch it. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Forge him a new one to match

ok.log: He tests it on a hanging gourd and grins. "This one bites the other fellow." (+120 taels)

fail.log: It is a good sword. He keeps the old one anyway. (+40 taels)

events.text: A grey-faced steward hires your agency to carry a sealed black-lacquer coffin to the capital, nine hundred li, for a fee that would buy a house. The coffin is not to be opened. It is very heavy, and on the first night, it knocks.
events.arc: The Jade Coffin to the Capital

choices.text: Take the job

effects.log: The coffin goes on the strongest cart. Your guards draw lots for who sleeps nearest it. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Refuse it

effects.log: The steward takes his coffin to the Golden Lion Agency. You hear later that they never reached the capital.

events.text: Night on the road at Seven Bends Gorge. The coffin knocks three times, and from the trees comes an answering whistle. Masked riders are coming down the slope.
events.arc: The Jade Coffin to the Capital

choices.text: Fight them off

roll.foeName: the masked riders of Seven Bends

ok.log: They break against your guards and scatter into the gorge. One of them shouts a name as he flees, a prince's name.
