fail.log: You hold the cart, barely. Two of your guards are wounded. The riders leave a token behind: a prince's seal.

choices.text: Open the coffin

effects.log: Inside is not a body but a boy of ten, very much alive, with a cup of water and a prince's jade pendant around his neck.

events.text: The boy in the coffin, or the name the riders shouted, can only mean one thing: a young prince smuggled out of exile, and his uncle's men on the road behind you. The capital is four days away.
events.arc: The Jade Coffin to the Capital

choices.text: Deliver him to the palace gate as promised

ok.log: He goes through the Meridian Gate on your cart at dawn. Within the month his uncle is in a cell, and your banner has an imperial ribbon on it. (+300 taels)

fail.log: The uncle's men catch you at the river. The prince escapes in the confusion, on foot, and reaches the palace alone. Nobody pays you.

choices.text: Hide him and take him somewhere safe instead

effects.log: You turn the cart west. The boy grows up in a mountain village, far from thrones, and seems happier for it.

events.text: At the mouth of Tiger Pass your senior guard, Old Fang, wants to cry out the agency's name, the old custom: a respectable agency announces itself and pays a toll in courtesy. The young guards think it is ridiculous and want to sneak through.
events.arc: The Old Call at Tiger Pass

choices.text: Let Old Fang call it

ok.log: His voice rolls up the pass. After a long silence, a voice rolls back: "Pass, and our respects to your house."

fail.log: Old Fang's voice cracks on the high note. Somebody up the pass laughs, but they let you through.

choices.text: Sneak through by night

ok.log: You are through by dawn, without a toll. Old Fang does not speak for a day. (+30 taels)

fail.log: Arrows out of the dark. The bandits of Tiger Pass do not like being snuck past.

events.text: The bandit chief of Tiger Pass, a one-eyed woman called Iron Plum, sends a messenger to your agency. She has a cargo of her own to send south, and she wants an agency with manners.
events.arc: The Old Call at Tiger Pass

choices.text: Take the bandit chief's cargo

effects.log: It is tea, honestly bought. She just cannot get it past the magistrates herself. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Decline politely, with a gift

effects.log: She sends back the gift with a note: "Manners indeed." Your carts pass Tiger Pass free for years. (-20 taels)

events.text: Iron Plum is old now and wants to leave the mountain. She offers you her road: the pass, her people and a promise that nobody will be robbed there again, if you will give them honest work.
events.arc: The Old Call at Tiger Pass

choices.text: Hire her people as guards

effects.log: Forty former bandits in your agency's colours. Nobody on the road dares touch your carts.

choices.text: Help her settle, but keep your agency clean

effects.log: She buys a small farm. Her people scatter. Tiger Pass gets a new bandit chief the next year.

events.text: Your agency is hired to escort a bride from the coast to her marriage in the north: twelve carts of dowry and one very quiet young woman called Lin Yue in a red sedan. On the third night she asks whether you have ever wanted to run away.

choices.text: Say yes, honestly

effects.log: She laughs for the first time. She asks about the road, every road, all night.

choices.text: Say a guard does not run

effects.log: She closes the curtain of her sedan and does not open it again.

events.text: Lin Yue is gone from her sedan at dawn, with one bundle and none of the dowry. The note says: thank you, and forgive me. Her husband's family is waiting at the next town.

choices.text: Track her down and bring her back

ok.log: You find her at a ferry. She comes back without a word, and the wedding goes on. (+100 taels)

fail.log: She is gone, into a country of a thousand ferries.

choices.text: Tell the family she fell ill and died of fever on the road

ok.log: You deliver the dowry, a story and a borrowed funeral. They believe you.

fail.log: They do not believe you, and you pay the penalty. (-100 taels)

events.text: Years later a letter comes, in a careful hand, from a town on the western border: Lin Yue has a tea stall, a husband who sings badly and two children, and she owes you everything.

choices.text: Write back

effects.log: You write back about the road, every road. The letters continue for twenty years.

choices.text: Send her a wedding gift at last

effects.log: A bolt of red silk, to make up for the one she left behind. (-20 taels)

events.text: A young guard called Zhao the Lucky, cocky as a rooster, swears he can take a cargo of medicine to the next prefecture alone, faster than any old guard.
events.arc: The Rookie and the Sleeping Smoke

choices.text: Let him try

effects.log: He rides off at a gallop with the cargo and your second-best horse.

choices.text: Send Old Fang with him

effects.log: Zhao the Lucky sulks for twenty li and listens for the next two hundred.

events.text: Zhao the Lucky comes back on foot without the cargo. A friendly old man shared his fire on the road, and his tea, and then Zhao woke up in a ditch at noon. It was sleeping smoke, an old trick of the road.
events.arc: The Rookie and the Sleeping Smoke

choices.text: Dock his wages until it is paid

effects.log: It will take him three years. He works every one of them. (+30 taels)

choices.text: Go after the old man with him

roll.foeName: the old trickster of the post road

ok.log: You find the old man selling your medicine in a market two towns over. Zhao the Lucky asks to tie the knots himself.

fail.log: The old man is gone, and so is the cargo. You pay the client. (-60 taels)

events.text: Zhao the Lucky, older now, is your best guard. He teaches every new recruit the same lesson first: never drink a stranger's tea, and never sit downwind of a friendly fire.
events.arc: The Rookie and the Sleeping Smoke

choices.text: Make him a senior guard

effects.log: Your agency loses fewer cargoes to tricks than any on the road.

choices.text: Send him to open a new route

effects.log: He opens the river route to the south, and is very careful about tea. (+60 taels)

events.text: The Golden Lion Agency across town has started telling clients that your agency lost three cargoes last season. You lost one, and it was not your fault.

choices.text: Publish your ledgers at the guild hall

ok.log: Your record is better than theirs and now everyone knows it. The Golden Lion's master is furious.

fail.log: Nobody reads ledgers. Everyone repeats rumours.

choices.text: Challenge the Golden Lion to escort the same cargo

effects.log: Two carts of the same silk, two banners, one road. The whole town wants to see it.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: Some clients go to the Golden Lion. Some come back.

events.text: The race. Both carts reach Black Water Ford on the same evening, and the river is in flood.

choices.text: Cross at once

ok.log: Your cart makes it across, water to the axles. The Golden Lion waits for morning.

fail.log: The river takes a wheel. The Golden Lion crosses in the morning past your broken cart.

choices.text: Wait for morning and help the Golden Lion's cart too

effects.log: You arrive together. The client pays both. The Golden Lion's guards buy you dinner.

events.text: The master of the Golden Lion comes to your gate with a jar of wine and an unusual proposal: a joint banner for the long routes, where no single agency is strong enough.

choices.text: Agree

effects.log: Two lions on one banner. Bandits take one look and go home. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Refuse, but share his supper

effects.log: You stay rivals, the friendly kind.

events.text: A grain merchant hires you to move rice to the western towns. Your senior guard tells you, quietly, that under the rice sacks the carts are full of untaxed salt.

choices.text: Refuse to move it

effects.log: The merchant shrugs and finds another agency. His carts are stopped at the first checkpoint.

choices.text: Move it for double

effects.log: You do not ask, and he does not tell, and the silver is heavy. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Report it to the Salt Commission

effects.log: The commission pays a reward and seizes the salt. (+50 taels)

events.text: A Salt Commission inspector stops your carts on the west road and looks at the rice for a very long time.

choices.text: Offer him a gift

effects.log: He accepts the gift and leaves the sacks closed. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Talk your way through

ok.log: He waves you on. You do not breathe until the next hill.

fail.log: He cuts a sack open. Salt pours out onto the road, white as an accusation. (-100 taels)

events.text: The grain merchant's friends burn one of your carts in its shed. A note on the gate says that people who talk to the Salt Commission should be careful.

choices.text: Hire more guards for the yard

effects.log: The yard is guarded night and day. Nothing else burns. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Go and have a word with the grain merchant

ok.log: The word is short. The merchant leaves town.

fail.log: The word goes badly. Another cart burns that week.

events.text: A jade trader offers a fortune to escort his caravan west beyond the Jade Gate, through forty days of desert where no agency of yours has ever gone.
events.arc: The Western Road Through the Sand

choices.text: Lead it yourself

effects.log: Camels, water skins, a guide called Old Ma who smells of goats. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Turn it down

effects.log: Some roads are better left to people who were born on them.

events.text: Day eighteen. A brown wall rises on the horizon and swallows the sun. Old Ma says one word: storm.
events.arc: The Western Road Through the Sand

choices.text: Circle the camels and wait it out

ok.log: A day and a night of sand. When it passes, every camel and every man is alive, half buried.

fail.log: When it passes, three camels and all the water are gone.

choices.text: Race for the rocks Old Ma swears are ahead

ok.log: The rocks are there, a red ridge with a cave. The storm howls past outside.

fail.log: There are no rocks, or they have moved. The storm finds you in the open.

events.text: No water. Old Ma says there was a well at a ruined fort two days east, twenty years ago.
events.arc: The Western Road Through the Sand

choices.text: Trust Old Ma

ok.log: The well is there, under a broken wall, full of bitter water. Nobody has ever tasted anything better.

fail.log: The well is dry. You dig with your hands until it is not. It takes a day you will remember for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Turn back the way you came

effects.log: You come home alive with half the camels and none of the fee. (-120 taels)

events.text: The caravan comes through the desert into a green city of poplars and blue-tiled gates beyond the Jade Gate. The jade trader pays you, then offers to buy everything you can bring next year.
events.arc: The Western Road Through the Sand

choices.text: Open the western route

effects.log: Your agency is the only one that runs the sand road. It is dangerous and it is rich. (+300 taels)

choices.text: Take your fee and never go again

effects.log: You come home with a sunburn, a camel and a story. (+150 taels)

events.text: A thin scholar with one robe and a box of books asks whether your next convoy to the capital can take him for nothing. He is going to sit the imperial examinations and has spent his last silver on ink.
events.arc: A Poor Scholar on the Capital Road

choices.text: Take him along

effects.log: He rides on the cargo, reading. At night he teaches the guards to write their names.

choices.text: Charge him half

effects.log: He pays in copper, and thanks you, and reads all the way. (+5 taels)

choices.text: Say no

effects.log: He walks. You pass him on the road two days later, limping.

events.text: Bandits stop the convoy on the last night before the capital. The scholar clutches his box of books as if it were gold.
events.arc: A Poor Scholar on the Capital Road

choices.text: Fight

roll.foeName: the bandits on the capital road

ok.log: They flee. The scholar has not let go of his box the whole time.

fail.log: You drive them off at a cost. The books are safe; your arm is not.

choices.text: Pay them off

effects.log: They take the silver and ride off. (-60 taels)

events.text: A procession with a red banner stops at your agency's gate. The thin scholar placed first in the palace examination, and he has come back as Top Scholar, in a red robe, to bow to the people who carried him.
events.arc: A Poor Scholar on the Capital Road

choices.text: Bow back, deeply

effects.log: The story of the Top Scholar who rode on an escort cart spreads through the whole province. Clients ask for "the scholar's agency".

choices.text: Ask him for a favour at court

effects.log: He arranges a court contract for your agency, honestly and without fuss. (+150 taels)

events.text: Old Fang, your senior guard for twenty years, takes an arrow in the knee on the south road. He will walk again, the physician says, but never ride guard.

choices.text: Pay for the best physician

effects.log: He grumbles at the needles and the bitter tea. He walks by spring. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Treat him yourself, with what you know

effects.log: You set the knee and brew the tea yourself. He complains about your hands every day, and walks by spring.

events.text: Old Fang cannot stand being idle. He sits in the yard all day criticising the young guards' stances.

choices.text: Make him the agency's instructor

effects.log: The young guards hate him for a season and love him for a lifetime.

choices.text: Give him a pension and a fishing rod

effects.log: He fishes, and criticises the fish. (-30 taels)

events.text: Old Fang dies in the yard on a spring morning, sitting on his bench, with his stick across his knees and a young guard practising in front of him. Every guard who ever served under him comes to the funeral.

choices.text: Carve his name on the gate

effects.log: Fang Lao, who never lost a cargo. The young guards touch it before every road.

choices.text: Name the new recruits' training after him

effects.log: Fang's Forty Days. Every guard of your agency goes through it.

events.text: The coastal salt towns need escorts, but the coast belongs to pirates in the summer. A branch office in Quanzhou would cost a great deal and could make your name.

choices.text: Open it

effects.log: A rented warehouse on the waterfront, a new banner and six guards who can swim. (-150 taels)

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: The coast can wait. The pirates certainly will.

events.text: Pirates of the Red Sail board a cargo junk you are escorting along the coast, at dawn, out of a sea fog.

choices.text: Fight on the deck

ok.log: You put three of them over the rail and the rest jump. The whole coast hears that your agency does not give up a ship.

fail.log: They take half the cargo and leave you tied to the mast. It is a long day.

choices.text: Surrender the cargo and save the crew

effects.log: Nobody dies. The client is furious. The crew are not. (-80 taels)

events.text: The Red Sail's captain sends a message by a fishing boy: a meeting, on neutral ground, a fish market at dawn.

choices.text: Go, and make a truce

ok.log: A toll, a handshake and a promise: your banner sails free. (+100 taels)

fail.log: The talk goes badly. You leave the fish market at a run.

choices.text: Go, and bring the coast guard

effects.log: The captain is taken. The coast is quieter. The Red Sail has a long memory.

events.text: A ragged young swordsman pawns his sword for ten taels and a bowl of noodles. He asks for ten years, not the usual one. On the ticket he writes no name, only: I will come back for her.
events.arc: The Sword Pawned for Ten Years

choices.text: Give him ten years

effects.log: You wrap the sword in oiled cloth and put it on the top shelf. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Give him one year, as the rules say

effects.log: He nods, as if he expected it, and goes out into the rain. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Refuse the pawn

effects.log: He looks at the sword a long time, then walks out with it into the rain, hungry.

events.text: A collector offers you two hundred taels for the sword on the top shelf. Its steel, he says, is from the old Southern Tang armouries. There are four years left on the ticket.
events.arc: The Sword Pawned for Ten Years

choices.text: Sell it

effects.log: The collector carries it away in a silk case. The ticket stays in your drawer. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: The collector raises his offer twice and leaves angry. The sword stays on the shelf.

events.text: The tenth spring. A swordsman in a plain grey robe walks into your shop with a famous name and a ten-tael ticket, and his hands are shaking.
events.arc: The Sword Pawned for Ten Years

choices.text: Give him the sword

effects.log: He unwraps it, and laughs, and weeps. He is the Grey Crane of Mount Heng now. He tells every hall in the murim about the pawnshop that kept its word.

choices.text: Charge him ten years of interest

effects.log: He pays it without a blink and bows. It was fair. (+120 taels)

events.text: The tenth spring. A swordsman in a plain grey robe hands you a ten-tael ticket. You open your mouth to explain, and he sees the empty shelf.
events.arc: The Sword Pawned for Ten Years

choices.text: Tell him the truth and give him the two hundred taels

effects.log: He takes the silver, then gives it back. "I wanted her, not money." He walks out. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Say the sword was stolen

ok.log: He believes you. That is the worst part.

fail.log: He finds the collector within the month. Then he finds you. The murim hears all about it.

events.text: A girl of twelve pawns a silver hairpin with a little jade bird on it. It was her mother's, she says. Her father is sick and the medicine costs eight taels.

choices.text: Give her twelve taels, more than it is worth

effects.log: She counts it twice, bows to the floor, and runs. (-12 taels)

choices.text: Give her the usual price

effects.log: Six taels. Not enough. She takes it anyway. (-6 taels)

choices.text: Send her to the temple physician instead

effects.log: She goes, clutching the pin. You do not see her again.

events.text: The redemption date for the jade-bird hairpin has passed. The girl has not come back. A rich lady sees the pin in your case and wants to buy it at once.

choices.text: Sell it

effects.log: The lady pins it into her hair at the counter. (+40 taels)

choices.text: Keep it a while longer

effects.log: You put it back in the drawer. Some rules can bend.

choices.text: Go and find the girl

effects.log: Her father died in the spring. She is selling vegetables in the east market. She cries when she sees the pin.

events.text: The girl with the jade-bird hairpin is a young woman now, with a market stall of her own. She lays twelve taels on your counter, and twelve more.

choices.text: Give her the pin and refuse the interest

effects.log: She tells the whole east market. Your pawnshop becomes the one the poor trust.

choices.text: Take it all

effects.log: She is happy to pay. She has her mother's pin. (+24 taels)

events.text: The girl from the east market brings her little brother to you. He is clever with numbers, she says, and would you take him as an apprentice.

choices.text: Take him on

effects.log: He can value a pearl at a glance by the time he is fifteen.

choices.text: Give him a letter for a merchant house instead

effects.log: He goes to the silk guild with your letter and does very well.

events.text: A nervous young man in a servant's jacket pawns a square bronze seal. You turn it over. It is the official seal of the county magistrate.

choices.text: Take it, and send for the constables

effects.log: He runs before they come. You keep the seal behind the counter, wrapped, as if it might bite.

choices.text: Refuse it and say nothing

effects.log: He goes pale and leaves. You wonder for weeks where it went.

choices.text: Take it and keep it quiet

effects.log: A magistrate's seal is worth more than silver to the right person. (-20 taels)

events.text: The magistrate's household is in uproar: without his seal, no orders, no taxes, no verdicts. Then a quiet man from the rival faction at the prefecture visits you, and asks about seals.

choices.text: Sell it to him

effects.log: He pays in gold. Within a month the magistrate is dismissed for losing it. (+300 taels)

choices.text: Return it to the magistrate

ok.log: The magistrate nearly embraces you. You are now, very unofficially, the most protected business in the county.

fail.log: He thanks you and has you arrested for receiving stolen property, to be safe.

events.text: The magistrate comes to your shop in person, without his escort. The servant who stole his seal has confessed. The magistrate would like to know why you sent for the constables when you could have sold it.

choices.text: Say a pawnshop has rules

effects.log: He leaves a calligraphy scroll that says "Honest Scales". It hangs in your window.

choices.text: Ask him for a favour in return

effects.log: He arranges for your licence to be renewed for ten years at no fee. (+60 taels)

events.text: Unclaimed goods day. In the false bottom of a brocade box pawned and forgotten thirty years ago you find a folded map: a mountain, a waterfall, and the seal of the Kunlun Sect.

choices.text: Follow the map

effects.log: You close the shop for a month and buy a mule.

choices.text: Sell the map to a treasure hunter

effects.log: A one-eyed treasure hunter buys it without bargaining, which worries you. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Take it to the Kunlun Sect

effects.log: A long road west, to a sect at the edge of the world.

events.text: The waterfall on the map, three weeks into the mountains. Behind it, a cave mouth, a stone door, and old carvings of swords pointing inward.

choices.text: Go in

ok.log: An empty tomb, a dead master's notes and a manual written in a cramped, brilliant hand.

fail.log: A trap of falling stones. You come out with a bruised shoulder and a broken lantern, and nothing else.

choices.text: Mark the place and go home

effects.log: Some doors are better left closed until you know who closed them.

events.text: At the edge of the world, the Kunlun Sect's elders look at the map in silence. It is the way to the tomb of their founder's brother, lost for two hundred years.

choices.text: Give it to them

effects.log: They escort you home with honour. Kunlun disciples bring their pawns to no one else.

choices.text: Ask for a reward

effects.log: They pay generously and a little coldly. (+200 taels)

events.text: The one-eyed treasure hunter is back, furious and missing two fingers. The map led to a trap. He wants his money and more.

choices.text: Give him his money back

effects.log: He snatches it and spits on your floor. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Refuse: he bought a map, not a treasure

ok.log: He leaves faster than he came in.

fail.log: He takes it from your strongbox himself. (-80 taels)

events.text: Your appraiser, Old Qian, has valued jade for forty years. Today he paid a hundred taels for a Song dynasty landscape painting. You hold it to the window. The paper is new, under the tea stains.

choices.text: Say nothing to Old Qian

effects.log: You take the loss yourself. Old Qian does not know. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Show him, gently

effects.log: He holds it close to his face for a long time. Then he puts on his spectacles, which he has never worn in front of you.

events.text: The forger, encouraged, is back with another Song landscape, and another, at other pawnshops in town. Old Qian wants to catch him.

choices.text: Set a trap with Old Qian

ok.log: The forger walks in with a fourth painting. Old Qian, in his spectacles, looks at it and says: "Lovely. Constables, please."

fail.log: The forger smells it and runs, with another of your loans. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Let the other pawnshops deal with it

effects.log: They do not. The town is flooded with fakes, and nobody trusts paintings for a season.

events.text: Old Qian retires. He leaves you his magnifying glass, his ledger of every fake he ever caught, and his advice: "Look at the paper, not the picture."

choices.text: Hire his granddaughter as appraiser

effects.log: She is as sharp as he was, and already wears spectacles.

choices.text: Learn appraisal yourself

effects.log: You spend a year at his ledger. You never buy a fake again, or almost never.

events.text: Young Master Wei of the great Wei house pawns a jade belt, then a silver incense burner, then his grandfather's chess set. Every week he comes, smiling, with something else.
events.arc: The Prodigal of the Wei House

choices.text: Keep taking his pawns

effects.log: The back room fills with Wei heirlooms. (+60 taels)

choices.text: Write to his father

effects.log: You write carefully, so as not to insult anybody. Nothing happens for a month.

events.text: Old Master Wei arrives in person, with four servants, and stands in front of his grandfather's chess set in your window.
events.arc: The Prodigal of the Wei House

choices.text: Sell it back to him at the loan price

effects.log: He buys back everything his son pawned, at cost, and looks at you the way one looks at a friend.

choices.text: Sell it back at the market price

effects.log: He pays without a word. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Tell him his son is welcome to redeem it

effects.log: He goes red, then pale, then home. That night there is shouting in the Wei house.

events.text: Young Master Wei comes in with a sack of copper earned, he says, by working in a cousin's rice warehouse. It is three years later and he is thinner. He would like his grandfather's chess set back, please.
events.arc: The Prodigal of the Wei House

choices.text: Give it to him

effects.log: He carries it home in both arms. His father, you hear, wept.

choices.text: Play him one game first

ok.log: He loses, laughs and thanks you. He has learned more than chess.

fail.log: He wins. He is very good. He takes his set home.

events.text: A celadon jar, pawned by a traveller who never came back, has started humming at night. The shop boy will not sleep in the shop. You listen: it is a low note, like a monk chanting very far away.

choices.text: Call a monk to listen to it

effects.log: The monk listens all night, very happily. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Put your ear to it yourself

ok.log: There is a tiny crack near the base. When the wind blows through the shutters, the jar sings.

fail.log: It hums all night in your ear. You dream of monks.

events.text: The town has heard of the singing jar. People come to listen to it, and some of them leave money for the singing jar's blessing.

choices.text: Put a donation box beside it

effects.log: The jar earns more than the shop. (+40 taels)

choices.text: Give the jar to the temple

effects.log: It sings in the temple now, in the evening wind. The temple is very pleased.

events.text: The traveller who pawned the jar comes back, five years late, and hears it singing in the evening wind.

choices.text: Return it, and the money it earned

effects.log: He is so astonished that he leaves you the jar. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Explain that it is past its date

effects.log: He pays you to listen to it once more and leaves. (+20 taels)

events.text: The Pawnbrokers' Guild sets the interest at three fen in the tael a month, which is ruinous for the poor. Its master notices that you have been charging two.

choices.text: Keep charging two

effects.log: The guild master smiles a thin smile and writes something down.

choices.text: Raise it to three

effects.log: Your customers grumble. They have nowhere else to go. (+60 taels)

events.text: The guild expels you. Your seal is no good at any other guild shop, and the guild's toughs hang around your door.

choices.text: Stand at your door with a staff

ok.log: They go. The poor of the district start sitting on your step, very obviously, as a guard of their own.

fail.log: They break your window and your counter.

choices.text: Petition the prefect

ok.log: Your petition is so well written that the prefect lowers the guild rate for the whole prefecture.

fail.log: The prefect's secretary is a guild member. Nothing happens.

events.text: The guild master is old and has lost a son to debt. He comes to your shop one night alone and sits for a long time before he speaks. The guild will lower its rate, he says, if you will come back.

choices.text: Come back to the guild

effects.log: Two fen in the tael, everywhere in the prefecture. The poor call it your rate.

choices.text: Stay outside, on your own terms

effects.log: He nods. The guild lowers its rate anyway.

events.text: A young monk pawns his begging bowl, the only thing he owns, for enough silver for a boat passage home to his dying teacher. He will redeem it, he says, with the alms of a year.

choices.text: Lend it to him without taking the bowl

effects.log: He stares at you, then laughs, then cries. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Take the bowl

effects.log: He leaves it reverently on your counter. It is a plain wooden bowl. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Tell him the shop does not take holy things

effects.log: He bows and walks out to beg his passage on the docks. You hear later that he reached his teacher a week too late.

events.text: Without his bowl the young monk has had to beg with his hands. He comes back after a year with exactly fifteen taels in copper, every one of them given to him by someone who had little.

choices.text: Give him the bowl and refuse the copper

effects.log: He bows, takes his bowl, and leaves the copper in your donation box for the poor anyway.

choices.text: Take the copper

effects.log: Fair is fair. He thanks you for the lesson. (+15 taels)

events.text: Twenty years later an abbot from a famous temple in the south visits your shop with a plain wooden bowl. He tells his monks the story of the pawnbroker who lent without a pawn, every year, as a teaching on trust.

choices.text: Ask him to bless the shop

effects.log: He blesses it, and pays for his tea.

choices.text: Ask him what he learned

effects.log: "That a stranger can be kinder than a teacher," he says, "and a teacher kinder than a stranger." You think about it for a year.

events.text: An old lacquer box, unclaimed for years, holds no jewels, only letters: an official in the prefectural granary writing to a grain merchant about prices, about shortages, about how much of the famine relief each of them will keep.

choices.text: Take them to the censor

effects.log: The censor reads them twice and goes very quiet.

choices.text: Write to the official, offering to sell them back

effects.log: You send the letter by a boy who does not know what he carries.

choices.text: Burn them

effects.log: Some things are not a pawnbroker's business.

events.text: The official's men come at night, not with silver.

choices.text: Fight them off

ok.log: They go. The official pays, the next week, in silver this time. (+150 taels)

fail.log: They take the letters and break your arm and your counter.

choices.text: Run and hide the letters

ok.log: You go over the roofs to the censor's house. You should have gone there first.

fail.log: They catch you two streets away and take everything.

events.text: The granary official is dismissed and the famine silver found. The censor writes to the throne. The people of the prefecture never learn the name of the pawnbroker who started it, but the censor does.

choices.text: Accept the censor's friendship

effects.log: Doors open for you in the prefecture that used to be locked.

choices.text: Ask for nothing

effects.log: He insists on paying for your lantern oil for a year, which is very like him.

events.text: A palace eunuch in plum robes orders a bolt of yellow silk with a dragon woven in gold, for a prince's birthday. Under his breath he adds: five claws. Only the emperor may wear a dragon with five claws.

choices.text: Weave five claws as asked

effects.log: Your best weaver works with her lips pressed tight. The fifth claw is beautiful and terrifying. (+250 taels)

choices.text: Weave four, and say it was a mistake

effects.log: Four perfect claws. The eunuch looks at them for a long moment and says nothing. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Refuse the order

effects.log: The eunuch smiles thinly and takes his silver to another house.

events.text: The prince wore the five-clawed dragon at his birthday banquet. Within a week he is under house arrest for treason, and the Censorate is asking who wove the silk.

choices.text: Flee the province

effects.log: You leave with what you can carry. Behind you the censors seal your warehouse.

choices.text: Go to the Censorate and tell everything

ok.log: You name the eunuch and show the order. The censors are pleased to have a bigger fish. You go home shaken, with your head.

fail.log: They are not interested in who ordered it. (-200 taels)

events.text: The prince's banquet passes without scandal. Weeks later, a man in a plain robe comes to your warehouse. He is the prince himself, and he knows the dragon had four claws.

choices.text: Kneel and say nothing

effects.log: "You saved my neck," he says. Imperial orders follow for years, all of them with four claws.

choices.text: Tell him why

effects.log: He laughs bitterly: the eunuch was his uncle's man. He never forgets your name.

events.text: The house that took the eunuch's order is closed by the Censorate. Its owner is in a cell. Your refusal has become known; the palace now asks for a reliable silk house.

choices.text: Take the palace contract

effects.log: Every bolt you send is checked three times, claws counted. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Bid for the closed house's looms

effects.log: You take on its weavers too, who are very grateful to be out of trouble. (-100 taels)

events.text: In the silkworm villages along the canal, the worms are dying white and stiff on the mulberry trays. The farmers who sell you their cocoons say the year is lost.
events.arc: The White Sickness in the Worm Houses

choices.text: Pay them an advance anyway

effects.log: They can eat this winter. They will remember it. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Buy cocoons from the next province

effects.log: Dearer, further, and the farmers here watch your carts go by. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Look into the sickness yourself

ok.log: Damp trays, closed windows, a mould. Lime on the floors and air through the houses might save next year.

fail.log: You find nothing. You pay an advance to make up for it. (-50 taels)

events.text: Spring in the worm houses. The lime and open windows have worked in some villages and not in others, and the farmers ask you which villages to trust.
events.arc: The White Sickness in the Worm Houses

choices.text: Buy only from the healthy villages

effects.log: Your silk is the best on the canal this year. The sick villages grumble. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Pay for lime for every village

effects.log: By autumn every village is healthy. Your name is said in every worm house. (-40 taels)

events.text: The silkworm villages have a good year at last. The farmers you paid in the bad year bring their best cocoons to your warehouse first, before the other houses have even sent their buyers.
events.arc: The White Sickness in the Worm Houses

choices.text: Pay the full price

effects.log: The best silk on the canal, and farmers who would walk through fire for you. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Pay a little less, since you helped

effects.log: They accept. Some of them stop smiling at you. (+140 taels)

events.text: Your weavers have stopped their looms. Their spokeswoman, a grey-haired weaver called Aunt Ruan, says their wages have not risen in ten years, while the price of silk has doubled.

choices.text: Raise their wages

effects.log: The looms start again by evening. Aunt Ruan nods to you on her way in. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Hire new weavers

effects.log: The new weavers are cheap and slow. Aunt Ruan's weavers stand outside your gate. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Sit down with Aunt Ruan and the ledgers

ok.log: You show her the books. She shows you what the weavers eat. You agree on a share of every bolt sold.

fail.log: She does not trust your books. You raise the wages anyway. (-80 taels)

events.text: A rival silk house tries to hire Aunt Ruan and her best weavers away.

choices.text: Trust them to stay

ok.log: They stay. Aunt Ruan tells the rival that she does not move looms twice.

fail.log: Half of them go. The rival's silk improves overnight.

choices.text: Make Aunt Ruan a partner

effects.log: Her name goes on your sign under yours. Nobody in the weaving quarter leaves you again. (-50 taels)

events.text: The new weavers' silk is uneven, and a merchant from the capital returns a whole order. Aunt Ruan's weavers are still standing outside your gate.

choices.text: Take them back at the old wage plus more

effects.log: They come back in silence. It takes a year for the jokes to return. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Close the gate on them

effects.log: They open a cooperative across the canal and take your best customers.

events.text: Merchants from the western kingdoms, men in tall felt hats who speak through an interpreter, want silk, as much as you have, and pay in horses, glass and silver coins with strange kings on them.

choices.text: Sell them a whole season's stock

effects.log: Every bolt goes west. The local houses complain that you have emptied the market. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Send a caravan of your own west

effects.log: Twelve camels, a guide and your best buyer. (-150 taels)

events.text: Your caravan reaches the oasis city of the western merchants. They will pay three times the price, the buyer writes, but they want a colour that does not exist yet: the blue of the sky after rain.

choices.text: Ask the dyers at home to find it

ok.log: Indigo, woad, a pinch of something from the south. It takes a year. It is perfect.

fail.log: The dyers try for a year. They come close. Close is not enough.

choices.text: Sell what you have at double

effects.log: Double is still very good. (+300 taels)

events.text: Sky-after-rain blue silk reaches the western kingdoms. Their queen wears it to a festival. The next caravan carries a letter from her court with an order that will take your looms three years to fill.

choices.text: Take the order

effects.log: Your silk house is known on the far side of the deserts. (+500 taels)

choices.text: Take half, keep the colour rare

effects.log: Scarcity is its own silk. (+250 taels)

events.text: The Duchess of Wu, a famous beauty and a famous tyrant of tailors, returns six bolts of your silk. Each has a flaw, her steward says. You cannot find a single one.
events.arc: The Duchess Who Sends Everything Back

choices.text: Take them back and refund her

effects.log: The steward takes the silver and a sample. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Ask to see the flaws

ok.log: The duchess sees you herself. There are no flaws. She wanted to meet the house that wove them.

fail.log: The steward is offended. The duchess tells her friends your silk is poor.

events.text: The duchess wants a gown for the Mid-Autumn banquet at the capital, in a pattern nobody has ever seen. She gives you a month and no other instructions.
events.arc: The Duchess Who Sends Everything Back

choices.text: Weave the moon over water

ok.log: She wears it, and the whole court falls silent. For a year every great house wants moon silk.

fail.log: She wears it and says it was "adequate". She pays. (+50 taels)

choices.text: Weave something safe and lovely

effects.log: She accepts it. She does not order again. (+80 taels)

events.text: Your old dyer, Master Pei, guards a secret blue: the colour of the sky after rain. Every great house wants it. Pei is seventy and has no children.

choices.text: Ask him to teach an apprentice

ok.log: He chooses the shyest boy in the dye house, and teaches him in the dark, by hand, without words.

fail.log: He says secrets die with their owners, as they should.

choices.text: Leave him be

effects.log: He goes on making blue. The days go on passing.

events.text: A man from the rival Hong silk house is caught climbing over the dye-house wall at night with an empty jar.

choices.text: Hand him to the constables

effects.log: The Hong house denies everything. Master Pei laughs for the first time in a year.

choices.text: Fill his jar with ordinary indigo and let him go

effects.log: The Hong house spends a season trying to make sky out of ditch water.

events.text: Master Pei dies in the winter. In the spring the shy boy holds up a length of silk to the window: sky after rain.

choices.text: Make the boy master dyer

effects.log: He bows, and cannot speak, and goes back to his vats.

choices.text: Name the colour Pei Blue

effects.log: It is still called that, in the markets, long after you are gone.

events.text: Master Pei dies in the winter, and the blue dies with him. Customers come and ask for it, and go away with lesser blues.

choices.text: Try to find it yourself

ok.log: After two years and a hundred vats, you find something close. You call it Pei's Ghost.

fail.log: You never find it.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: Some colours are only lent.

events.text: The Supervisor of the Imperial Silk Office, a soft-voiced eunuch called Chamberlain Mo, explains that palace orders come with a small gratitude: one tenth of the price, to him.

choices.text: Pay the tenth

effects.log: The palace orders come thick and fast. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: Chamberlain Mo smiles. The palace orders go to the Hong silk house.

events.text: Chamberlain Mo wants more: a fifth now, and a nephew of his on your payroll.

choices.text: Pay

effects.log: The nephew sleeps in the warehouse and draws a wage. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Go over his head to the Empress Dowager's household

ok.log: An old lady-in-waiting who loves your silk mentions it to the Dowager. Chamberlain Mo is transferred to the imperial stables.

fail.log: Chamberlain Mo hears of it first. Your palace orders end. (-50 taels)

events.text: Chamberlain Mo has fallen, as eunuchs fall: suddenly, at night, with his ledgers. The new Supervisor asks every silk house whether it paid him.

choices.text: Say no, truthfully

effects.log: The Hong house said no, untruthfully. The palace orders come back to you.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: The new Supervisor writes your silence down.

events.text: The court astrologer has declared next spring the luckiest season for weddings in sixty years. Every family in the province wants red silk at once.

choices.text: Buy every red dye in the province now

effects.log: Madder, safflower, cinnabar: your warehouse is the colour of a festival. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Plan to weave only what you can

effects.log: You plan the year calmly.

events.text: Spring. Weddings everywhere. Red silk is worth its weight in silver, and the poor families cannot afford a single bolt for their brides.

choices.text: Sell it all at the high price

effects.log: Your strongbox has never been so heavy. (+300 taels)

choices.text: Sell to the poor at the old price

effects.log: Brides from the poor quarters wear your red. Every one of them remembers. (+100 taels)

events.text: Spring. Weddings everywhere, and your looms are never still. A matchmaker in the market suggests a small red sash for every bride, cut from the end of each bolt.

choices.text: Give the sashes away to brides

effects.log: A red sash from your house becomes lucky. Families come to you for the bolts, too.

choices.text: Sell the sashes

effects.log: They sell like hot buns. (+60 taels)

events.text: Your newest weaver, Little Ning, is quick and quiet, and spends her evenings copying your pattern books by lamplight. She says it is to practise.

choices.text: Watch her

ok.log: Every tenth day she takes a parcel of copies to the back gate of the Hong silk house.

fail.log: You see nothing but a hardworking girl. Perhaps that is all she is.

choices.text: Leave her be

effects.log: She is the best weaver you have had in years.

events.text: Little Ning knows she has been seen. She stands before you shaking: the Hong house holds her brother's debt, and she is paying it with your patterns.

choices.text: Pay the debt and keep her

effects.log: She weeps, and works for you for thirty years. She never copies a pattern again. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Dismiss her

effects.log: She leaves. The Hong house stops getting your patterns.

choices.text: Give her false patterns to carry

effects.log: The Hong house weaves a whole season of your deliberately ugly patterns. Nobody buys them.

events.text: Your newest patterns appear at the Hong silk house's stall before you have even woven them.

choices.text: Change all the patterns and say nothing

effects.log: It costs a season. The leak stops, or moves. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Confront the Hong house

ok.log: Their master blusters, then pays. The town enjoys it.

fail.log: They laugh and say they thought of it first. The guild agrees with them.

events.text: The most famous opera singer in the province, Yu Feiyan, who sings the Drunken Concubine and the Farewell to the King, sends a messenger: she needs new robes for her autumn season.
events.arc: The Opera Star in Your Silk

choices.text: Make them for free, for the advertisement

effects.log: Your weavers work on nothing else for a month. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Charge her the full price

effects.log: She pays without a word. Stars always do. (+120 taels)

events.text: Opening night. Yu Feiyan sweeps on stage in your silk, and the whole house rises. In the morning there is a queue at your door for the Feiyan colour.
events.arc: The Opera Star in Your Silk

choices.text: Weave nothing but the Feiyan colour

effects.log: For a year every lady in the province wears it. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Keep it exclusive to her

effects.log: She tells everyone in the opera world that your house is the only one worth wearing.

events.text: Yu Feiyan, older now, gives her farewell performance. She sends you a front-row ticket and, after the last bow, the robe she wore that first autumn.
events.arc: The Opera Star in Your Silk

choices.text: Hang it in your shop

effects.log: People come to look at it for years. It is the most beautiful thing in the shop.

choices.text: Give it to the opera school

effects.log: Young singers wear it for their first performances, for luck.

events.text: The Lantern Festival is coming, and the merchants' street will judge the best stall: the winner's sign hangs at the head of the street all year. Last year the Plum Pavilion won with a lantern shaped like a carp the size of a boat.

choices.text: Build a lantern taller than the carp

effects.log: A paper phoenix, two storeys high, built in your yard by three very nervous carpenters. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Hang a hundred lantern riddles, a prize for each answer

effects.log: You spend a week writing riddles. Some of them are very bad. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Do not bother this year

effects.log: You watch the festival from a bench with a bowl of sweet dumplings, which is also a fine way to spend it.

events.text: Festival night. The wind rises at the second watch.

choices.text: Hold the phoenix steady

ok.log: The phoenix sways and glows over the whole street. Children cry when it is taken down. You win.

fail.log: The phoenix catches fire, very beautifully. Everyone agrees it was the best thing at the festival. The judges do not.

choices.text: Let it go and see what happens

effects.log: It sails off over the river like a real phoenix, burning, and lands in a paddy. People talk about it for years.

events.text: Festival night. Your hundred riddles draw a crowd three deep. A boy of ten answers forty of them in a row and wants forty prizes.

choices.text: Give him all forty

effects.log: He leaves with a sack of sweets and a reputation. The crowd adores you. You win the street. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Give him one hard riddle more

ok.log: He thinks for an hour and gives up, delighted. He comes back every year to try again.

fail.log: He answers it at once. The crowd roars. Maybe he should write your riddles.

events.text: An old friend from your youth, now a prosperous tea broker called Fat Ming, slaps a purse on your counter: he wants to put money into your business, as a partner, for the old days.

choices.text: Take the silver and make him a partner

effects.log: He signs the contract with a flourish and orders wine for everyone. (+200 taels)

choices.text: Thank him, and refuse

effects.log: He is a little hurt and very relieved. You stay friends.

events.text: Fat Ming has opinions now. He wants to change the sign, double the prices, and hire his nephew, who is 'very good with numbers'.

choices.text: Give way on the nephew

effects.log: The nephew is very good with numbers, especially other people's.

choices.text: Buy him out

effects.log: It costs more than he put in. It is worth it. You are still friends, mostly. (-250 taels)

choices.text: Argue it out over tea

ok.log: By the third pot he agrees to everything you wanted and you agree to a new sign. Business is good.

fail.log: By the third pot you are both shouting. The staff take sides.

events.text: The nephew has vanished with the strongbox key and the money in it. Fat Ming arrives at dawn, grey-faced, with his own purse in his hand.

choices.text: Take his purse to cover the loss

effects.log: He insists. You let him. It is the end of the partnership, but not of the friendship. (+150 taels)

choices.text: Tell him to keep it

effects.log: He cries into his sleeve. You are friends until one of you dies.

events.text: One of your children, {npc}, has started spending afternoons in the business, sweeping, carrying, listening to the customers haggle. Today the child corrected a customer's sums, out loud, in front of everyone.

choices.text: Give the child a little job

effects.log: A small stool behind the counter and a small abacus. The customers start asking for the young clerk.

choices.text: Send the child back to study

effects.log: The child goes, sulking, with a book. You notice the book is about trade.

events.text: Your child {npc} has made a mistake: a large order taken on credit from a man who does not exist. The loss is real.

choices.text: Cover it quietly

effects.log: You pay it and say nothing, and the child knows, and never forgets. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Make the child work it off

effects.log: A year of the worst jobs in the business. The child grumbles and learns.

events.text: {npc}, grown now, sets a plan on your desk: a new branch, new suppliers, a new way of keeping the books. It is better than anything you have ever done.

choices.text: Let the child run with it

effects.log: It works. The business grows. People start calling you the old owner.

choices.text: Say not yet

effects.log: The child folds the plan very carefully and keeps it. One day.

events.text: The business came to you with the family, and its staff came with it. The old head clerk, Uncle Sun, served your parent for thirty years. Today he hands you the keys with the face of a man waiting to be disappointed.
events.arc: The Staff Who Knew Your Parent

choices.text: Ask him to teach you everything

effects.log: He blinks. Then he takes you through the ledgers line by line, for a month, with a cane he uses to point.

choices.text: Tell him things will be done your way now

effects.log: He bows. He says nothing. The staff say a great deal, quietly.

events.text: Uncle Sun finds an error in your first year's books: in your favour, and against an old supplier your parent always treated well.
events.arc: The Staff Who Knew Your Parent

choices.text: Pay the supplier back

effects.log: Uncle Sun nods, for the first time, as if you might do. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Keep it: business is business

effects.log: Uncle Sun writes it down in his own little book. (+40 taels)

events.text: Uncle Sun retires. On his last day he gives you a letter your parent left with him, to be given to the heir when the heir was ready.
events.arc: The Staff Who Knew Your Parent

choices.text: Read it at once

effects.log: It says very little: be fair to the small suppliers, and trust Sun. You read it many times.

choices.text: Keep it sealed for a hard day

effects.log: It sits in your desk. Knowing it is there helps on hard days.

events.text: Madam Hong, the busiest matchmaker in town, has started holding her meetings in your corner booth: two families, two nervous young people, a pot of your best tea and a great deal of silence.
events.arc: The Matchmaker in the Corner Booth

choices.text: Give her the booth for a small fee

effects.log: She pays and keeps coming. (+20 taels)

choices.text: Give it to her for free and keep the tea coming

effects.log: She tells every family in town that your teahouse is lucky for matches.

events.text: A disastrous meeting: the young man's mother and the young woman's grandmother turn out to have quarrelled over a goose forty years ago. Voices rise. A teacup flies.
events.arc: The Matchmaker in the Corner Booth

choices.text: Step in with a new pot and a story

ok.log: You tell them a funny story about a goose. Both old women laugh despite themselves. The young people look at each other properly for the first time.

fail.log: The cup breaks, the meeting breaks, and Madam Hong sighs into her sleeve. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Leave it to Madam Hong

effects.log: She has seen worse. The match fails. She tries again next week with another family.

events.text: The young couple from the goose meeting are married. They hold the betrothal tea in your corner booth, and Madam Hong, very pleased, brings you a red envelope.
events.arc: The Matchmaker in the Corner Booth

choices.text: Accept it

effects.log: Matches made in your booth become a fashion. (+30 taels)

choices.text: Give it to the couple as a gift

effects.log: They name their first child after the teahouse, which is a little strange but very sweet.

events.text: A year without rain. The farmers need new ploughshares to break the hard ground for a late planting, and they have nothing to pay with but promises.

choices.text: Forge on credit

effects.log: Forty ploughshares, forty promises in your ledger. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Forge only for cash

effects.log: Six farmers can pay. The rest go home. (+20 taels)

events.text: The rain comes late, and the farmers with your ploughshares are the only ones whose fields are ready for it.

choices.text: Collect your debts at harvest

effects.log: They pay in rice and silver and gratitude. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Forgive the poorest families

effects.log: The village builds a little shrine to the smithy god by your gate. (+60 taels)

events.text: Bandits come down on the village after the harvest. The farmers do not run. They come to your forge for spear-heads, and then they stand together at the bridge.

choices.text: Stand with them

ok.log: The bandits look at forty farmers with new iron and a smith with a hammer, and decide to rob somewhere else.

fail.log: It is a hard fight. The village holds. You carry a scar from it, and they carry you home.

choices.text: Forge the iron and let them fight

effects.log: You forge through the night. The iron holds; so does the village. (-20 taels)

events.text: A tiny old man with a white beard and a donkey hires your agency to escort him to Mount Song. He pays well, in old silver. Your guards whisper that he is Monk Hui Ming, once the strongest fist in the murim, who has no need of guards at all.

choices.text: Take the job and treat him like any client

effects.log: He seems delighted to be treated like any client. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Ask him why he needs guards

effects.log: "To see how you do it," he says, and climbs onto his donkey.

events.text: On the road the old man criticises everything: the guards' stances, the way they hold their spears, the way they look at the trees. Then bandits come out of the trees.

choices.text: Defend him as if he were helpless

ok.log: Your guards close around the donkey and drive the bandits off. The old man claps.

fail.log: It goes badly, until a pebble from somewhere knocks the bandit chief flat. The old man is looking at the sky.

choices.text: Ask the old man to help

effects.log: He does not move. "I hired you," he says. Your guards fight alone, and win, barely.

events.text: At the gate of Shaolin on Mount Song the old man climbs off his donkey and turns to your guards. He will give each of them one lesson, he says, for doing their jobs.

choices.text: Let him teach them

effects.log: One lesson each, an hour each. Your guards come home and fight like a different agency.

choices.text: Ask for a lesson yourself

effects.log: He teaches you one movement, for a whole afternoon. You use it for the rest of your life.

events.text: A ship's captain on the river offers you silk at half the price: woven in the south, untaxed, unstamped and very fine.

choices.text: Buy it

effects.log: You sell it at your own price under your own stamp. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: He shrugs and sails on.

choices.text: Tell the river customs

effects.log: The customs officers thank you. The captain will not.

events.text: A customs officer, very polite, is going through every silk house's stock, matching stamps against the tax registers.

choices.text: Pay him to look elsewhere

effects.log: He looks elsewhere. You look at your empty purse. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Hide the bolts in a temple

ok.log: The monks are very puzzled by their new silk curtains. Nobody finds anything.

fail.log: The temple is the first place he looks.

events.text: The ship's captain is caught downriver. His ledger has the names of every silk house that bought from him. Yours is not one of them, and the customs commissioner says so publicly.

choices.text: Thank the commissioner

effects.log: Honest silk houses are suddenly in great demand.

choices.text: Buy the seized silk at the customs auction

effects.log: Legally, this time, and cheap. (+80 taels)

events.text: Once a year the unclaimed pawns go out on tables in the street for anyone to buy. This year there is a whole table of things nobody wants: one boot, a broken lute, a cage with no bird and a scroll of bad poetry.

choices.text: Sell it all for a copper each

effects.log: A crowd of children buys the lot and runs off laughing. (+15 taels)

choices.text: Look through the strange table yourself

ok.log: Inside the broken lute, wrapped in silk, is a jade token from the Imperial Music Bureau.

fail.log: It is all exactly what it looks like. The poetry is very bad.

events.text: The jade token from the broken lute leads you to an old blind musician in a back street, who once played for an emperor and pawned his lute in a hungry winter.

choices.text: Have the lute mended and give it back

effects.log: His fingers find the strings. He plays for an hour without stopping. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Sell him the token back

effects.log: He pays with the last of his coins. (+20 taels)

events.text: The blind musician plays every evening now, on your pawnshop steps, for anyone who stops. People stop. Some of them come in.

choices.text: Pay him a wage

effects.log: The Pawnshop With Music. People bring their heirlooms just to hear him. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Let him keep what the listeners give

effects.log: His bowl fills every night. He plays you something special on your birthday.
